n01b28a89df77: Replication timing (RT) coordinates DNA synthesis with genome organization and influences mutation rates, cancer evolution, and developmental plasticity. Current methods infer S-phase timing from DNA content, an assumption that obscures responses to replication perturbations and limits accurate comparisons of RT changes. Here, we develop 2C-RT, a multiplexed sequencing approach that uses DNA content-independent markers for robust RT profiling across S phase. Combining 2C-RT with imaging, we resolve distinct layers of human RT control and identify local and genome-wide responses to drugs and genetic perturbations. We find that RIF1 spatially restricts CDC7 activity and that its loss does not neutralize RT per se but advances replication across most RIF1-sensitive regions. A conserved MCM5 bob1 mutation lowers the origin-activation threshold and reveals a role for CDC7 in establishing local origin dominance. These findings support a revised model in which CDC7 primes early origins, CDK promotes permissive origin firing genome-wide, and RIF1 counteracts CDC7 in distinct chromatin states and peripheral nuclear domains. ### Competing Interest Statement S.E. and P.Y.K hold patents for multiplexed ChIP technology. S.E. co-founded Epigenica AB, a start-up within Karolinska Institutet incubator for commercialization of multiplexed epigenetics profiling tools. Rest of authors declare no competing interests. ncc913675cff9: Individual human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) particles can differ in their envelope protein (Env) despite being genetically identical. This non-genetic diversity can influence antibody recognition and has been implicated in the formation of persistent virus fractions that escape complete inhibition by broadly neutralizing antibodies. Investigating non-genetic diversity in HIV and other viruses requires approaches capable of characterizing antibody binding to individual viral particles. Flow virometry provides a promising tool for single-particle analysis, but a system combining high biosafety with specific particle labeling and versatility is lacking. Here, we developed a third-generation lentiviral vector system specifically designed for flow virometry. Fluorescent proteins were incorporated into the HIV-1 Gag polyprotein between the matrix- and capsid-encoding regions, flanked by viral protease cleavage sites, creating the packaging constructs pLentiFlow-eGFP and pLentiFlow-mCherry. Lentiviral particles (LVPs) based on pLentiFlow vectors were fluorescent and retained infectivity comparable to LVPs generated with the parental vector system despite reduced particle production. We optimized LVP detection on a CytoFLEX nano and defined a linear p24-based concentration range for reliable single-particle analysis. Using complementary controls, we demonstrated that background from the assessed sources accounted for no more than approximately 3% of events within a broad eGFP+ gate and confirmed that the detected fluorescent particles were predominantly membrane-enclosed. As a proof of concept, LVPs were pseudotyped with vesicular stomatitis virus glycoprotein, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 spike, or HIV-1 Env. Envelope-specific antibody binding was detected using 8G5F11, CR3022 or PGT128, respectively, demonstrating that different viral surface proteins can be analyzed on a common particle backbone. Together, these results establish a third-generation lentiviral vector system for flow virometry that combines intrinsic particle labeling with high biosafety and flexible pseudotyping. The system provides a platform for investigating envelope protein-associated non-genetic diversity and its consequences for antibody recognition in HIV and other viruses.
nf69e40d3a7ca: The value of rhodopsin proton pumps as light harvesters in electro-microbial CO2-to-biomass conversion depends on molecular photophysics, pathway energetics and reactor light delivery. We couple these scales for Cupriavidus necator, comparing Calvin-Benson-Bassham (CBB) and reductive glycine (rGlyP) assimilation. The model predicts a 17.9% dark rGlyP yield advantage, close to 16.5% measured in chemostats. At 568 nm, 100 PPFD and 45% membrane occupancy, light-derived ATP raises yield by 17% for rGlyP and 14% for CBB. Charging CO2 capture and formate electrosynthesis, a retinal-only reactor reaches 3.29% efficiency versus 2.56% in the dark. A carotenoid antenna raises this to 3.52% at the model-derived 70% transfer estimate and helps in 93.2% of uncertainty samples, but lowers efficiency at the thermodynamic limit by diverting photons from photovoltaics. Point-source CO2 cuts the relative light benefit from 38% to 8%. Rhodopsin is therefore most useful when upstream formate is energy-intensive, not as a general efficiency boost.
n18bb83b1c66f: The neurodevelopmental metabolic shift transitions the energy sources and metabolic pathways used by neurons to critically support survival, growth, and the timing of functional maturation. To better understand metabolic regulation during human neuronal development, and to facilitate the study of early neurodevelopmental disorders impacting this time window, establishing a combination of effective human model systems will be required. We report that a streamlined strategy using genetic induction of neuronal differentiation by NGN2 expression recapitulates hallmarks of metabolic reprogramming associated with neuronal maturation. The approach is refined to increase the uniformity of differentiation, allowing reproducible high-throughput assessments. We validate appropriate readouts of metabolic function, including gene expression, cellular respiration, and mitochondrial imaging which can be combined to present a cohesive assessment of metabolic status and reliance on oxidative phosphorylation relative to glycolysis. Collectively, the strategy presented will enhance the ability of investigators to gather foundational and disease-related insights into regulatory mechanisms of the metabolic shift critical to successful neuronal differentiation. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. National Institutes of Health, https://ror.org/01cwqze88, R01MH129292, T32 5T32GM144272 Braude Foundation
n749fc6cf6724: Characterization of naturally processed MHC class I (MHC-I)-bound peptides is essential for defining allele-specific peptide-binding features and understanding the functional consequences of MHC-I polymorphism. However, immunopeptidome analyses of dog leukocyte antigen (DLA) class I (DLA-I) molecules remain limited and comprehensive monoallelic ligand datasets for prevalent DLA-88 alleles are still lacking. Here, we established canine melanoma-derived cell populations expressing individual functional DLA-88 alleles and generated a monoallelic immunopeptidome atlas of prevalent DLA-88 alleles. Using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, we identified 32,702 naturally processed peptides of 7 to15 amino acids across 10 DLA-88 alleles, substantially expanding the available DLA-88 immunopeptidome landscape. These 10 alleles exhibited canonical peptide length distributions and allele-specific binding motifs that reflected variation in binding-groove pseudo-sequences defined from human MHC-I peptide-contact residues. Ligand sharing between DLA-88 alleles was associated with binding site distance. Incorporation of the comprehensively characterized DLA-88 ligand datasets in this study increased by more than fourfold the number of published canine DLA-I alleles with ligand-characterized reference alleles predicted to have similar peptide-binding features. We also found that antigen-processing signatures were highly conserved with those reported in humans. As a proof-of-concept application, we selected 54 DLA-88-bound peptides identified in our immunopeptidome analysis as candidate peptides for canine cancer immunotherapy by evaluating the normal tissue expression profiles of their source proteins. This DLA-88 immunopeptidome atlas provides insights into allele-dependent differences in antigen presentation and represents a valuable resource for developing accurate DLA-88-binding peptide prediction tools and supporting peptide-based immunological studies in dogs.
nccf9205093de: Large-scale genetic and preclinical studies strongly implicate myeloid cells, particularly brain-resident macrophages, in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Efferocytic clearance of apoptotic cells and other cholesterol-rich cellular debris is a core macrophage function and represents an active area of AD research. However, human tissue-resident macrophages remain difficult to model in vitro as they acquire their transcriptional and functional identities in response to signals from their host tissue microenvironment. Many existing differentiation protocols mimic human brain macrophage developmental trajectories, but these protocols rely either on multi-step cytokine cocktails and lengthy differentiation or transduction of multiple transcription factors, both of which introduce variability and complicate genetic manipulation. To address these limitations, we developed a simplified protocol that generates high-purity (>90% CD45+CD11b+) human iPSC-derived macrophage-like cells (iMacs) from cryopreservable erythro-myeloid progenitor (EMP)-like intermediates in 19 days, including a final 7-day maturation step driven by macrophage colony-stimulating factor (M-CSF) alone. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that iMacs show enrichment for phagocytic and lysosomal programs, processes integral to efferocytosis. At both the transcriptional and protein level, iMacs have higher expression of scavenger receptors such as CD36, CD163 and MRC1, and of AD risk genes such as TREM2. Functionally, iMacs show enhanced phagocytic uptake of diverse substrates relative to iPSC-derived microglia, including carboxylated latex beads, zymosan, amyloid-{beta} 1-42, and amyloid-{beta} 1-40, and exhibit expanded lysosomal mass. Robust TREM2 expression and signaling make iMacs a sensitive platform for interrogating TREM2 biology, with markedly higher phosphorylation of SYK and PLC{gamma}2 in response to TREM2 engagement compared to iPSC-derived microglia. iMacs also tolerate lipid-mediated siRNA transfection with high survival and knockdown efficiency, enabling rapid genetic perturbation of AD risk genes. Together, these features make iMacs a practical, scalable, and genetically tractable human macrophage model for studying the regulation and cell biology of core macrophage functions that are known to play critical roles in AD, aging, and other disorders.
n5b87f7d13b25: Quantifying interactions in biological tissues requires determining whether an interaction exists, the distance over which it operates, and its strength. Existing spatial-statistical approaches can characterize spatial organization but often require interaction range or interaction models to be specified a priori, making them less suited to settings where these quantities are themselves unknown. Here, we present a practical framework that recovers the presence, range, and association strength of spatial bias toward a tissue structure directly from segmented histology. The framework combines four complementary statistics, the resource selection function, nearest-structure distance distributions, the cross J-function, and the radial distribution function, with specimen-specific reference states that preserve tissue stromal architecture while spanning a continuum of known spatial biases. Across controlled in silico tissues, we show that tissue stromal architecture imposes geometric limits on the range of recoverable interactions and that event fraction independently constrains statistical sensitivity. These spatial associations establish fundamental bounds on inference and demonstrate that spatial statistics must be interpreted relative to tissue-specific reference states rather than absolute scales. We apply the framework to proliferating tumor cells relative to CAF-rich stroma during tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy in an ALK+ NSCLC model and identify a strong stroma-associated proliferation bias extending approximately 30-60 micrometers. The framework broadly applies to any histological setting where events and reference structures can be defined, providing a practical approach to quantify localized interactions directly from tissue stromal architecture.
nb4257f2cff6b: DNA-PAINT enables super-resolution imaging with high multiplexing capacity, yet it is rarely used in nanoscale bacteriology. A likely reason is the lack of straightforward protocols and of systematic characterization of imager-docking strand pairs inside intact bacterial cells, whose envelope and dense cytoplasm differ markedly from both the DNA origami in vitro systems used to develop them, and eukaryotic cells. In this work, we establish a screening platform based on RNA-FISH, in which we extend the 16S rRNA-directed EUB338 probe with docking sequences of choice. This allows imager-docking pairs to be benchmarked directly inside Escherichia coli cells and characterized for parameters such as specificity, binding kinetics, and localization precision. We screened 12 different DNA-PAINT sequences and used an optimized set to perform four-target 3D Exchange-PAINT in single E. coli cells. We further applied our strategy to image three effector mRNAs in the Gram-negative pathogen Yersinia enterocolitica and quantified RNA clusters and their 3D distribution. Our work provides a framework and practical guidelines for high-quality 3D DNA-PAINT imaging in Gram-negative bacteria and should facilitate its broader adoption in nanoscale bacteriology.
n597cffb54caf: Recent advances have improved understanding of infection; however many detailed datasets are based on single timepoints post-infection and cannot generate longitudinal insights needed to predict infection outcomes. For example, pulmonary infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) initiates a complex system of immune and bacterial interactions that leads to granuloma formation, yet single snapshots in time need elaboration long-term. We develop a new approach, the tissue time machine, applied to predict outcomes of non-human primate granulomas from initiation to endpoint using single timepoint tissue datasets including high-dimensional spatial features. This involves identifying granuloma digital partners, simulations most closely resembling real granulomas from a virtual library of over 50,000. By analyzing digital partners, we predict infection outcomes of 22/28 granulomas, and that Mtb-specific, IFN-{gamma}-producing T cell recruitment rates influence uncertainty for the 6/28. This method is applicable to any system that allows for mechanistic predictions over time using heterogeneous, incomplete, and high-dimensional datasets.
nf152600489d3: Polycystin-1 (PC1) functions as an atypical G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) with an autocatalytic GAIN domain that cleaves PC1 into extracellular N-terminal (NTF) and membrane-embedded C-terminal (CTF) fragments. Mutations in PC1 are responsible for 85% of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) cases. Activation of signaling by PC1 CTF has been shown to be allosterically mediated by a stalk tethered agonist (TA) and to be prevented by mutations of the stalk. Soluble, synthetic peptides derived from the PC1 stalk were also shown to re-activate signaling by a stalkless CTF mutant. Here, we have investigated the ability of selected stalk peptide agonists p9, p15 or p17 to re-activate signaling by PC1 CTF with ADPKD-associated missense mutations, G3052R or R3063C. Biochemical experimental data showed that each of the three stalk peptides was able to significantly reactivate signaling by the CTF-R3063C mutant. In contrast, signaling by CTF-G3052R could only be rescued by treatment with p17. In parallel, we employed peptide docking and novel Peptide Gaussian-accelerated Molecular Dynamics (Pep-GaMD) simulations to elucidate the binding conformations of p9, p15 and p17 to the PC1 mutants. The simulation findings were highly consistent with experimental data. Furthermore, Pep-GaMD revealed binding conformations of the agonist peptides and important low-energy conformational states of the PC1 CTF, as well as their critical residue interactions. Overall, our complementary approach provides important mechanistic insights into the re-activation of PC1 disease-associated mutants by stalk-derived peptide agonists. Such insights are expected to be valuable for the future design and development of peptide modulators targeting PC1 for an effective ADPKD therapeutic treatment.
n171764e33667: In May 2026, an outbreak of hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) caused by Andes virus (ANDV) was detected aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius, sparking public health measures in multiple countries. ANDV infections in humans are mostly sporadic, most often linked to exposure to infected rodents in South America, although small clusters of human cases, like the 2026 outbreak on the MV Hondius occur as well. It is not known whether virological factors may contribute to this distinct epidemiology, and no phenotypic characterisation of the newly emerged ANDV (ANDV2026) has been carried out to date. Here, using an ANDV isolate from a presymptomatic patient from the MV Hondius, we studied pathogenesis, identified sites of viral replication, characterized innate and adaptive immune responses, and quantified shedding in golden Syrian hamsters. ANDV2026 proved to be highly pathogenic in hamsters, causing severe pulmonary disease reminiscent of HPS. ANDV2026 triggered a delayed type-I IFN response and inflammatory response in the lungs consistent with the key pathological features of HPS, and we detected viral replication in both respiratory and extra-respiratory tissues, including the brain. Infected animals mounted neutralising antibodies and T cell responses, the latter directed predominantly against the L and N proteins. Importantly, ANDV2026-infected animals shed virus through multiple routes, and we detected infectious virus in air samplers connected to cages housing ANDV2026-infected hamsters. In contrast, control hamsters infected with a rodent-derived ANDV isolate (ANDV9717869) shed little virus and air samples were consistently negative. These findings consolidate established features of ANDV pathogenesis, while revealing properties not previously described. Phenotypic characterisation of patient-derived ANDV isolates in animal models can strengthen outbreak preparedness, identify markers of disease severity, and support the development of medical countermeasures.
nf3095f0895ed: Cell-by-cell and gene-by-gene relationships, such as kernels and correlations, shape most single-cell analyses but are rarely inspected directly due to a lack of visualization tools that display them. AnnZarro is a point-and-click browser viewer that shows these matrices linked to an AnnData object's cells x genes data. Using AnnZarro, experimental biologists can explore data without code and computational biologists can probe the relationships behind their analyses. One focused cell and one focused gene drive every panel. Clicking a cell paints its row of any cell-by-cell matrix over an embedding or spatial coordinates; clicking a gene paints its row of any gene-by-gene matrix over a gene plot such as a volcano. The focus also links genes to the cells where they change, and cells to the genes that distinguish them. AnnZarro reads only the matrix rows and columns each panel displays from zarr stores and hence users can explore matrices far larger than memory on a laptop or a shared server. Large datasets open on a reproducible subset, and users step through the remaining cells in parts. On a laptop, a 100,000-cell part of Tahoe-100M opens in 4 s and stays interactive. With the subset switched off, AnnZarro draws all 95.6 million cells in one plot in about 5 to 7 s. This tutorial prepares a dataset with Kompot differential abundance and expression, a diffusion kernel and gene correlations, then explores it in six worked examples.
n11f3b92dc67e: Given the expenses associated with Parkinson Disease (PD), it is imperative to develop a method for accurate diagnosis before emergence of motor symptoms. While there are tests that can measure early onset of PD, these tests still rely on subjective input from patients and can thus be biased. Factors influencing their accuracy include environmental agents such as education and culture. Thus, blood-based transcriptomic signatures are a promising direction for biomarkers in PD that are minimally invasive and more objective than clinical evaluation. In this paper, we analyzed gene expression from the PPMI cohort. Using a Bayesian framework, a gene interaction network was constructed to enhance differential expressed genes (DEG) analysis through signal diffusion. In tandem with clinical traits, 13 genes were selected for optimal discrimination using a random forest model. Within the holdout test set, the model achieved an AUC of 0.972, outperforming contemporary models. The model performance demonstrates the potential of using blood-based transcriptomics to enhance clinical diagnosis of PD. Other genes recovered by network diffusion but missed by traditional DEG analysis are already validated as potential biomarkers in contemporary PD research. By combining transcriptomic signatures with clinical evaluation, accurate diagnosis of PD can happen before the major destruction of dopaminergic neurons, which is critical for effective intervention and treatment. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.
n40edc20cb5f6: Arsenic (As) is a widespread environmental contaminant, with exposure occurring primarily through contaminated food and water or cigarette smoke. Maternal exposure to As represents a significant risk factor for congenital heart disease in offspring. However, the mechanisms underlying As induced developmental cardiotoxicity remain poorly defined. Pluripotent stem cells provide an excellent platform for studying mechanisms of developmental toxicity. Embryoid bodies (EBs) derived from stem cells, can recapitulate many key events of early embryogenesis including germ layers specification. Human cardiomyocytes are derived from mesodermal progenitors. NKX2.5 governs cardiac specification and morphogenesis, and its mutation produces atrial and ventricular defects in humans. Using an NKX2.5 reporter stem cell line, we modeled mesoderm differentiation in EBs and cardiac induction in a 2D cardiomyocyte differentiation system. In an 8 day differentiation protocol, As (0.05 μM; 3.75 ppb) significantly suppressed cardiomyocyte differentiation and cardiac induction. However, As increased mesodermal markers (HAND1, SNAI2, HOPX) gene expression. In contrast, cardiac specific genes, including NKX2.5, GATA4, Troponin T, and alpha actinin, were markedly downregulated in the presence of As. As also reduced expression of genes related to cardiac induction, fibroblast function, and vascular markers in the cardiac organoid model. As impaired cardiomyocyte maturation related gene expressions at concentrations without affecting cardiomyocyte proliferation. In a zebrafish model of early heart development, As increased heart rate and disrupted ion channel gene expression. In conclusion, As inhibits ESC differentiation into cardiomyocytes and disrupts cardiomyocyte maturation. Combining stem cell derived models with zebrafish exposure, this study illuminates adverse outcome pathways for As induced congenital heart defect.
n5af7d2bc3baf: Cobalamin is a complex yet essential cobalt-containing cofactor synthesized exclusively by prokaryotes and archaea. Aerobic cobalamin biosynthesis requires the CobNST multi-subunit class I cobaltochelatase for cobalt incorporation. Cobalt chelation is dependent on the energy transfer from the CobST AAA+/VWA motor unit to the substrate-binding catalytic unit (CobN). However, the mechanism for assembly and function of CobNST cobaltochelatase remains poorly understood. Here, we used cryo-EM to solve the structures of the AAA+ motor CobS, in the absence and presence of ATP and its VWA-partner protein CobT. Our data reveal that the AAA+ CobS assembles into various conformations, including hexameric planar rings and different spiral left-handed assemblies: hexamers, double rings and filaments. In the absence of nucleotide, the CobT N-terminal domain interacts with CobS left-handed oligomers, remaining in a half-assembled, nonfunctional motor unit. In the CobST complex, ATP induces conformational rearrangement of CobS from left-handed helical oligomers to a right-handed closed hexamer. The simultaneous repositioning of the CobT VWA domain to the AAA+ central pore shifts the motor unit to a functional state, ready-to-drive CobN-catalyzed chelation reaction. These findings define the mechanism for assembly and activation of the class I cobaltochelatase CobST motor.
ne2a39c2c437a: Among women, urinary tract infection (UTI) represents a major health concern. Approximately 50% of the adult female population experienced an episode of UTI at least once. UTI and recurrent UTIs caused by resistant bacteria are very common in clinical settings. The treatment and management of UTI is becoming more challenging because of the rise in antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Lactobacillus spp are the dominant bacterial genus in urinary and vaginal microbiota, which are also used as probiotics. In this study, Lacticaseibacillus paracasei SRG isolated from the vagina of healthy women were evaluated for its probiotic-associated properties and cell-free supernatant (CFS)-mediated antibacterial activity against eight uropathogens. The antibacterial activity of CFS was concentration- and pH-dependent, which was significantly evident at CFS/2 and CFS/4 concentrations and acidic pH values of 4 and 5. The antibacterial activity in CFS remains unaltered even after heat and proteinase K treatment, which suggests the role of heat- and protease-resistant metabolites beside the contributions from acidic conditions. L. paracasei SRG showed strong autoaggregation (85.32%) and cell-surface hydrophobicity (55.60%). In addition, it also exhibits co-aggregation with all indicator strains, suggesting substantial interaction with diverse pathogenic bacteria. These observations highlighted the L. paracasei SRG as a potential probiotic candidate developed from indigenous vaginal microbiota.
nfe1e8374d21e: Population-scale gut microbiome reference databases exist for Western and East Asian cohorts, yet no harmonised healthy baseline has been available for India's 1.4 billion inhabitants, whose diets span extreme geographic and cultural gradients. Western-derived reference ranges risk systematic misclassification when applied to Indian subjects. We harmonised eight published Indian healthy-gut microbiome cohorts (1,672 samples from 1,456 unique individuals , 20 geographic locations, six zones) onto a common NCBI family-level taxonomy axis. Raw 16S rRNA amplicon data were reprocessed through a uniform QIIME 2 / DADA2 / SILVA 138.1 pipeline where raw sequences were available; author-provided taxonomic tables from MetaPhlAn, HITChip, and RDP-based pipelines were retained and mapped via a four-step resolution cascade (exact match, synonym lookup, genus-to-family fallback, Unassigned). We defined the Indian Gut Health Index (IGHI), a four-component composite score (diversity, taxon balance, core membership, community typicality) calibrated against geography-stratified healthy Indian norms. The unified matrix comprised 380 bacterial families, of which 17 constituted the pan-Indian core ([≥]80% prevalence; Lachnospiraceae 100%, Prevotellaceae 99.5%). PERMANOVA confirmed significant compositional differences across geographies (pseudo-F = 43.4, p = 0.001) and cohorts (pseudo-F = 89.6, p = 0.001). Variance partitioning revealed that geography and cohort effects were deeply confounded (shared variance 30.4%; pure geography 4.1%, pure cohort 4.7%, residual 60.9%). Restricted permutation PERMANOVA confirmed city-level geographic signal after cohort correction (p = 0.001), but zone-level signal did not survive (p = 0.896). Two community types were identified: a Prevotellaceae-dominant type (69%) and an Oscillospiraceae-dominant type (31%), contrasting with the Western three-enterotype model. A Random Forest zone classifier achieved 68.4% balanced accuracy (null 16.6%), with Northeast subjects most distinguishable (F1 = 0.92). IGHI zone means ranged from 67.6 to 72.9 (inter-zone range 5.3 points), confirming effective geographic normalisation. Weight sensitivity analysis showed IGHI rankings were robust to moderate perturbation (Spearman {rho} [≥] 0.88 for five of six alternative schemes). The BioMeBarTM Indian Gut Reference Atlas provides the first pan-Indian harmonised healthy microbiome baseline, and the IGHI offers a population-calibrated scoring framework for gut health assessment in Indian individuals. The atlas, scoring model, and analysis code are openly available at https://github.com/TusharParihar128/BioMeBar_Indian_Healthy_Cohorts_datasets.
n7ed83a8f1942: The endocannabinoid system is comprised of bioactive lipids that signal via cannabinoid receptors, which can modulate barrier and immune functions along the gastrointestinal tract. Clinical studies indicate that endocannabinoid activity is dysregulated in inflammatory bowel diseases. Here, we show that endocannabinoid activity promotes metabolic dysfunction within the colonic mucosa, resulting in microbial dysbiosis and exacerbated colitis. Stimulation of the cannabinoid receptor CB1 resulted in the expansion of Enterobacteriaceae within the gut microbiome, a common feature of inflammation-associated dysbiosis. Preceding this microbial change, CB1 activity induced transcriptional signatures of mitochondrial stress and immune activation within the colonic mucosa. This was followed by a reduction in mucosal ATP production and the induction of aerobic respiration genes in luminal Escherichia coli. Genetic inactivation of aerobic respiration in E. coli limited its proliferation, indicating that CB1 activity stimulates oxygen-dependent Enterobacteriaceae growth. In IBD susceptible mice, endocannabinoid activity promoted mucosal infection by an E. coli pathobiont, which corresponded with elevated pro-inflammatory markers. In inflammation resistant mice, acute CB1 stimulation was sufficient to accelerate the infection dynamics of an Enterobacteriaceae pathogen, resulting in exacerbated colitis. Taken together, our data support a model in which endocannabinoid signaling at the CB1 receptor disrupts respiratory metabolism in the colon, compromising the anoxic environment of the lumen that is critical for maintaining aerobically respiring pathogens at low abundance. More broadly, our findings highlight a proinflammatory effect of endocannabinoid activity that can contribute to intestinal disease development.
ne6a8bdfd4f61: RpoS, an alternative sigma factor, directly regulates approximately 10% of gene transcription in E. coli. The small protein Crl functions as a partner that assists RpoS in exerting its regulatory role, particularly during the stationary phase. However, the coordinating role of Crl during the exponential phase remains unclear. In addition, whether Crl can regulate gene transcription independently of RpoS is still unknown. Therefore, in this study, we used the RpoS-dependent operon hdeAB and the RpoS-independent operon proVWX as model systems to investigate the transcriptional regulatory function of Crl using RT-qPCR and 3C-qPCR. Since the expression of both Crl and RpoS is modulated by environmental signals, we further examined the transcription of these operons under different pH and osmotic conditions. The results showed that Crl can regulate transcription independently of RpoS and exhibits environment-specific bidirectional regulation. Overall, this study improves our understanding of the regulatory mechanisms of Crl and highlights the complexity of transcriptional regulation.
nb4f973ea1ff5: Nullomers are sequences absent from a certain genome. Due to their unexpected occurrence in short sequences, a hypothesis is that they are avoided for evolutionary reasons or because they might have lethal consequences on organisms. However, we present evidence that the occurrence and frequency of nullomers in genomes is expected as a stochastic consequence of uneven base pair combination distributions in the genetic code. This is done by artificially constructing whole genomes from statistics with a Markov chain model. The number of nullomers in these artificial genomes is in good agreement with the nullomer counts in reference genomes. Additionally, we investigated the nullomers of over 200 human genomes and found large deviations in the nullomers between individuals, further supporting the hypothesis that a vast majority of nullomers is very unlikely to have lethal effects.
n3c9e66c612bd: Purpose: Subretinal fibrosis causes irreversible vision loss in neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) and remains poorly controlled by anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) therapy. We investigated the role of B-crystallin (CRYAB) in angiogenic and fibrotic pathology and evaluated disease-associated CRYAB truncation as a therapeutic target. Methods: Aqueous humor from patients with nAMD was analyzed by quantitative proteomics and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. CRYAB function was assessed using knockout and knockdown approaches in a choroidal neovascularization (CNV) mouse model. CRYAB truncation and associated proteins were examined by immunoblotting, co-immunoprecipitation, and liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). C-terminal truncation was further examined in mouse retinal tissue using antibodies generated against full-length CRYAB and its C-terminal region. Primary human retinal pigment epithelial (hRPE)-THP-1 co-cultures were used to examine CRYAB truncation under fibrosis-associated conditions. Pharmacological effects were tested using ({+/-})-threo-3-methylglutamic acid (T3MG) and 4-(2-aminoethyl)benzenesulfonyl fluoride hydrochloride (AEBSF). Results: CRYAB was upregulated in the aqueous humor of patients with nAMD. Higher CRYAB levels were associated with persistent lesions after initial anti-VEGF treatment. CRYAB knockout or knockdown reduced CNV pathology and decreased VEGFA and -smooth muscle actin (SMA) expression, without a significant substrain effect between C57BL/6N and C57BL/6J mice. A Ser45-phosphorylated truncated CRYAB species was detected in mouse laser-induced CNV model. We termed this species disease-associated truncated CRYAB in AMD (DTCAMD). Peptide mapping showed reproducible loss of distal C-terminal peptide coverage in truncated CRYAB. Consistent with this finding, C-terminal antibody recognition was reduced in CNV lesions. In hRPE-THP-1 co-cultures, DTCAMD accumulated with increased SMA expression. Proteomic analysis identified Prss1 as a candidate CRYAB-associated serine protease linked to truncation under CNV conditions. T3MG and AEBSF reduced DTCAMD-associated signals and CNV pathology. Conclusions: CRYAB contributes to angiogenic and fibrotic pathology in CNV. Disease-associated CRYAB truncation, particularly Ser45-phosphorylated DTCAMD, represents a potential therapeutic target for fibrotic remodeling in nAMD.
na6b1ebeb5a2a: Bexarotene (BEX), a retinoid X receptor (RXR) agonist, has demonstrated therapeutic potential in oncology, neurodegenerative diseases and inflammatory conditions, including multiple sclerosis (MS). However, its broader clinical application is limited by poor aqueous solubility, low bioavailability, and dose-limiting adverse effects, most notably hypertriglyceridaemia. In this study, we investigated whether conjugation of BEX to dextrin, a biodegradable polysaccharide, could improve its physicochemical properties and therapeutic index. A dextrin-BEX conjugate was synthesised using succinoylated dextrin (30 mol%) and characterised by gel permeation chromatography (GPC), Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance (1H-NMR) and dynamic light scattering (DLS). The effects of conjugation on solubility, aggregation behaviour and biological activity were evaluated using in vitro cytotoxicity assays in leukaemia, liver and fibroblast cell lines, alongside measurements of intracellular triglyceride levels. The impact on lipid metabolism and toxicity was further assessed in an in vivo murine model of hyperlipidaemia. Dextrin conjugation significantly increased the aqueous solubility of BEX (from <0.004 mg/mL to 9.88 mg/mL) and led to the formation of nanoscale aggregates in solution. This was associated with a marked increase in in vitro potency, with IC50 values reduced by up to 14-fold across multiple cell lines. However, the increased cytotoxicity was not selective for cancer cells and was also observed in normal fibroblast and hepatic cell models. The dextrin-BEX conjugate did not induce intracellular triglyceride accumulation in vitro. In vivo, dextrin conjugation did not mitigate BEX-associated lipid dysregulation, while serum triglyceride levels and markers of liver injury remained unchanged. However, although free BEX led to a significant increase in liver weight after 14 days, the dextrin-BEX conjugate did not produce a statistically significant effect. In conclusion, dextrin conjugation markedly improves the solubility and in vitro potency of BEX but does not enhance its selectivity or reduce its metabolic toxicity in vivo. These findings suggest that while polymer conjugation is an effective strategy for addressing physicochemical limitations, it is insufficient to overcome the inherent dyslipidaemia associated with systemic RXR activation. Future strategies should focus on integrating targeting and controlled release mechanisms, alongside approaches that address the underlying pharmacological drivers of lipid dysregulation.
n89f47bbb1510: Gut microbes metabolize nutrients in infant diets, producing compounds that play roles in host health. Long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids (LCPUFAs) are an important component of infant diets, supporting neurological development and immune regulation. Emerging evidence demonstrates that gut microbes, alongside the host, participate in the metabolism of dietary lipids, highlighting an underexplored avenue for LCPUFA biology. In this work, alkyne-tagged eicosapentaenoic acid (EPAALK) was used to investigate interactions between LCPUFAs and the gut microbiota. Flow cytometry and comparative metabolomics identified gut microbial EPA interactors in the ileum of mice. Further comparative metabolomics analysis identified the conversion of EPA to N-acyl amino acids, including attachment to phenylalanine (EP-Phe) and leucine (EP-Leu). Targeted analysis of ex vivo stool cultures determined that EP-Phe and EP-Leu are produced by gut bacteria. A survey of lipid-relevant infant gut bacteria determined various flow cytometry-confirmed EPA-microbe interactions and identified Enterococcus faecalis, Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron, and Clostridium bifermentans as competent producers of EP-Phe or EP-Leu. Thus, both novel metabolites from diet-derived inputs and microbial producers of these metabolites were identified. Together, this highlights important microbiome-centric and mechanistic consequences of LCPUFA consumption and emphasizes that the gut microbiome may be an important consideration in targeted supplementation strategies.
nad67e9209df9: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is highly polygenic, and the largest genome-wide association study (GWAS), with 53,660 cases and 2,044,417 controls, identified only 30 loci, a small fraction of loci estimated to explain its heritability - too few to resolve biological pathways. Pet dogs develop a compulsive disorder (dogCD) similar to OCD. In a GWAS of dogCD with 2,584 dogs from the community science project Darwin's Ark, each dog locus explains at least 40-fold more phenotypic variance than each human OCD locus, giving power equivalent to the human GWAS with 80-fold fewer individuals. Combining the two GWAS identifies a 165-gene network undetectable in humans at current sample sizes. This network is enriched for genes expressed in neurons, particularly in the amygdala and cortex, and comprises four biological processes: excitatory-inhibitory synaptic transmission, axon guidance and neuron recognition, protein ubiquitination, and adenylyl cyclase-activating G-protein-coupled receptor signaling. Like most complex human traits, dogCD risk is likely driven by regulatory variation: fine-mapped dogCD SNPs are non-coding, and dogCD loci are enriched in candidate cis-regulatory elements (cCREs) in a new dog epigenomic atlas spanning eight brain regions. The cross-species network implicates an inherited risk architecture largely outside current OCD pharmacotherapy, and establishes pet dogs as a model for gene network discovery, particularly for conditions underpowered in human studies.
n53adadc1aa02: Breast cancer is the most diagnosed cancer worldwide. Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a subtype with a poor prognosis because of its aggressiveness and high likelihood of relapse, making its treatment particularly challenging. We explored the effect of Tumor Treating Fields (TTFields) as a novel treatment option for breast cancer, which can be used together with other therapies, such as PARP inhibitors. TTFields use alternating electric fields to inhibit cell growth and induce cellular damage. Our findings indicate that TTFields increase expression of the universal cell cycle CDK inhibitory protein p21(WAF1)/CDKN1A independently of TP53 mutational status. Moreover, when used together with the PARP inhibitor talazoparib, the combination further upregulates p21 protein. Both TTFields alone and together with talazoparib induce cell death as documented by PARP cleavage while reducing markers of cell growth and anti-apoptotic proteins, including p-STAT3, STAT3, and MCL-1. Additionally, TTFields together with talazoparib induce DNA damage, as indicated by increased {gamma}H2AX expression. The combination of talazoparib plus TTFields treatment decrease PDL-1 levels and given its utility in predicting response to PD-1/PD-L1 by mediating immune evasion, this raises the possibility of future combination for immune modulation in cancer therapy. Our preclinical results suggest TTFields alone or together with PARP inhibitors such as talazoparib as a promising therapeutic approach for further development for the treatment of breast cancer.
n6f0cec2d087e: The effects of many genes and disease-associated variants remain hidden in standard cellular models, limiting functional interpretation. Here we engineer regulatory states via CRISPR activation of transcription factors (TFs) in human RPE-1 cells, a model for age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Multiome Perturb-seq profiling of single-TF perturbations identified regulators that selectively opened chromatin at AMD GWAS variants inaccessible in resting RPE-1. Priming of partner motifs in chromatin made accessible by single-TF perturbations predicted TF pairs generating emergent transcriptional states in combinatorial Perturb-seq, providing a design principle for selecting informative interactions. Distinct TF pairs also showed variable convergence between polygenic AMD signals and Mendelian retinal disease genes, supporting an omnigenic model shaped by regulatory states. Finally, Mosaic, a chromatin-informed model of TF interaction phenotypes, nominated out-of-sample regulators, including a higher-order combination with experimentally validated emergent effects on AMD-associated programs. Engineered regulatory states thus bring hidden disease biology within experimental reach.
n50444008c846: Seed number per pod is a major soybean yield-component trait, yet experimentally validated causal modules remain poorly defined. Here, we identify and functionally validate a soybean NAT-ULT regulatory module controlling ovule and seed number per pod. Through a visual screen of a fast-neutron-irradiated Glycine max cv. Williams 82 population, we isolated MO27, which increased four-seeded pod frequency from approximately 2-4% in wild type to 27-30%, without major changes in plant architecture, total pod number, or seed morphology. Comparative genome hybridization mapped the phenotype to a 46.7-kb chromosome 2 deletion containing GmNAT1 and chromosome 6 deletions encompassing GmULT-B1 and GmULT-B3. Ovule-clearing analysis showed that increased seed number originated before fertilization through elevated formation of four-ovule ovaries. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis of GmNAT1, GmULT-B1, and GmULT-B3 increased four-seeded pod frequency without detectable penalties in 100-seed weight, total pod number, or plant height. Tomato SlULT triple mutants also increased floral organ and locule number, supporting conserved ULT-like function in reproductive organ patterning. RNA-seq interaction analysis revealed a chromosome 6-dominant transcriptional state, accompanied by selective non-additive reprogramming of hormone/ovule-number and cell-wall-remodeling modules. Integrated genetic and transcriptomic analyses support a hierarchical model in which NAT-ULT perturbation may enhance meristematic competence and remodel reproductive developmental programs, while additional fast-neutron-background-associated transcriptional changes may further modulate the phenotype. These findings define NAT-ULT as a molecular target for engineering soybean seed number per pod.
nfe5e1ff96e56: Animals colonizing food-limited environments need to overcome growth constraints by adapting to low, inconsistent nutritional inputs. Comparative studies of surface and cave populations of the Mexican tetra fish species Astyanax mexicanus provide a powerful system to explore evolution to food scarcity. In nutrient-scarce caves, evolved traits such as eye loss and increased fat storage have been shown to conserve energy in cavefish 1-3 . However, the role of microbiota-mediated metabolism in sustaining growth and survival under food limitation remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that surface and cave populations distinctly modulate their gut microbiota, with cavefish recruiting microbes whose predicted metabolites specifically promote growth under nutrient-limited conditions. Using microbiota data from three distinct dietary regimes and a fasting treatment, integrated topological data analysis4 and sparse modeling identify sugar and fatty acid degradation pathways coupled with growth in cavefish. Notably, the metabolites of these pathways are beneficial only for cavefish growth, and not for surface fish. Fasting in cavefish led to the recruitment of gut microbes capable of metabolizing aromatic compounds inaccessible to the host, whereas it recruited few microbial associates in surface fish. Our findings indicate that cavefish evolved novel host-microbiota coupling to sustain growth and resilience in their nutrient-scarce niche. We anticipate that our findings will broadly inform studies of evolution under extreme nutritional conditions and provide insights into the role of host-microbiota interactions in resilience to food scarcity at varied time scales.
ncc1fb6fc26b5: The outer membrane protein W (OmpW) family comprises minor porins essential for environmental adaptation and host interactions in Gram-negative bacteria. However, ompW is conventionally treated as a ubiquitous single-copy gene, masking its true evolutionary complexity. Through comprehensive phylogenetic analysis across thousands of reference genomes, we reveal that ompW is present in nearly half of Gram-negative lineages, exhibiting a patchy distribution governed by a birth-and-death model of evolution with recurrent duplications and horizontal transfer. Notably, copy number expansions concentrate in lineages associated with eukaryotic hosts, linking paralog accumulation to niche adaptation. Experimental validation in Acinetobacter baumannii reveals four distinct loci that maintain high structural conservation despite sequence divergence, yet undergo profound functional specialization spanning from baseline physiological maintenance to modulating host colonization and persistence in vitro and in vivo. These findings dismantle the single-copy paradigm, demonstrating that widespread gene family expansion and paralog diversification drive the phenotypic plasticity required for bacteria to colonize hostile host environments.
nfc5922058a95: **Objectives:** Recurrent urinary tract infection (rUTI) is increasingly complicated by antimicrobial resistance (AMR), yet urinary microbiome dysbiosis and isolate-level resistance-virulence are rarely examined together across different treatment states. In this study, we characterized both within the same sample in rUTI and in healthy controls. **Methods:** In this cross-sectional cohort, mid-stream urine was collected from women with untreated, treated and prophylaxis rUTI and age-matched healthy controls at four centres in South India. Of 80 samples collected, 75 were analysed (26 controls, 20 untreated, 20 treated, 9 prophylaxis) by 16S rRNA V3-V4 sequencing. In addition, 105 culturable isolates from the same samples were identified and tested for antimicrobial susceptibility (VITEK 2) and phenotypic virulence. **Results:** rUTI groups showed approximately half the alpha diversity of controls (median Shannon 1.07-1.18 vs 2.17; Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.041). Community structure differed from controls in every rUTI subgroup (PERMANOVA R-squared = 0.091, p = 0.004; pairwise FDR = 0.008) but not among subgroups. Mean Lactobacillus relative abundance fell from 29.2% in controls to <=13.2% in rUTI groups, while Escherichia-Shigella rose from 7.2% to 25.0-43.0%. Control-referenced dysbiosis z-scores were elevated in all rUTI groups (community distance: FDR <= 0.003; uropathogen: Lactobacillus index: FDR < 0.001 for treated and prophylaxis groups). Among isolates, Escherichia coli predominated (35/105; 16/35, 45.7% multidrug-resistant), followed by Klebsiella spp. (32% multidrug-resistant); carbapenem susceptibility was largely retained, and multidrug-resistant E. coli co-carried more virulence traits. **Conclusions:** rUTI is associated with a stable dysbiotic state that treatment does not restore, combining Lactobacillus loss and uropathogen dominance with a multidrug-resistant culturable reservoir that co-accumulates virulence traits. Reading the community and its isolates together may support microbiome-sparing, resistance-aware management of rUTI.
nd5fddab016cb: Microbial communities in harsh environments such as the Canadian high Arctic, remain a relatively unexplored source of antimicrobial natural products. In this study, we developed a pipeline for screening and evaluating bacterial isolates cultured from 23 Canadian high Arctic soil, sediment, and active-layer permafrost samples to discover antibacterial compounds. The pipeline incorporated an undergraduate studentsourcing program and produced created a collection of over 350 bacterial isolates with preliminary antibacterial activity. Following dereplication, whole genome sequencing and secondary screening by co-culture assays, five isolates were prioritized to test crude extracts for antibacterial activity. Among bioactive crude extracts from these isolates, the Pseudomonas isolate with the most potent activity against S. aureus was analyzed. Using liquid chromatography bioactivity guided fractionation, we identified a potential bioactive compound known as koreenceine A, a compound previously only isolated from a Pseudomonas from temperate soil and involved in gene expression of other their microbial community. Here we expanded the known antibiotic activity of koreenceine A and confirmed that a {triangleup}kecBCD genetic knockout of the putative biosynthetic gene cluster significantly abrogated the antibacterial activity.
nefaba766e779: The Geoffroy's bat ( Myotis emarginatus ) is a sedentary species increasingly threatened by habitat alteration. Here, we assessed genetic diversity and population structure in 760 individuals from 18 French maternity colonies using 34 microsatellite markers and mitochondrial D-loop sequences. Mitochondrial data revealed subtle regional structure, consistent with female philopatry, and a broader phylogeographic split between Western Europe and the Greater Middle East, reflecting historical isolation. In contrast, microsatellites showed high nuclear diversity and minimal population structure across France, with weak isolation by distance and kin clustering, indicating extensive male-mediated gene flow. Moreover, demographic inference suggested population stability, consistent with both marker types. This nuclear homogeneity and demographic stability are strikingly similar to the patterns observed in Rhinolophus ferrumequinum populations sampled at the same colonies, suggesting that reproductive aggregation can maintain connectivity even in sedentary species. Overall, M. emarginatus functions as a largely connected population at the national scale, although localized maternal lineages suggest the presence of functional phylopatric units around key maternity sites that warrant protection. Future genome-wide studies could refine conservation strategies by integrating fine-scale female philopatry with male-mediated connectivity.
ne73f437aefe6: H1N1 influenza viruses have circulated continuously among human populations for five decades. During evolution, the hemagglutinin has accumulated amino acid substitutions in and around the receptor-binding site (RBS), mainly due to antigenic pressure, potentially altering receptor recognition and binding profiles. Here, we investigated the glycan-binding properties of H1N1 strains collected from 1977 through 2024 using ELISA, flow cytometry, and tissue histochemistry to characterize changes in receptor-binding specificity over time. Across the strains examined, we observe a recurring preference for binding 2,6-sialylated di-LacNAc N-glycans. Binding to 2,3-sialylated glycans was generally undetectable, although A/Hongkong/117/1977 and A/New Caledonia/20/1999 bind chicken tracheal tissues. Interestingly, post-pandemic H1N1 viruses fluctuate in their relative binding avidities. The responsible amino acids, in turn, have different effects in pre-pandemic HA proteins. We also report a classical egg-adapted H1N1 mutant that shows null binding across platforms. These findings highlight the contribution of RBS mutations during initial adaptation and evolution of human H1N1 influenza viruses to glycan-binding properties, which, in contrast to H3N2 viruses, never fail to bind glycans that correlate with avian erythrocyte hemagglutination.
n4ff3c6556121: Mechanical forces shape cell behaviour, yet how Piezo1-associated responses encode force magnitude, recent mechanical history and cytoskeletal context under repeated fluid shear remains unclear. We combined defined fluid shear stress (FSS) with GenEPi, a genetically encoded reporter of Piezo1-proximal Ca2+ entry, in engineered XLGenEPi-HEK293T monolayers to resolve mechanically evoked responses at single-cell and population scales. GenEPi responses increased with FSS magnitude but showed diminishing response gain at higher shear. Repeated submaximal FSS produced history-dependent attenuation and reduced temporal coordination, with higher FSS accelerating the early phase of attenuation. Low-dose Latrunculin A, without significantly reducing bulk F-actin abundance, converted sustained FSS-evoked signalling into a brief, decay-dominated response while largely preserving peak responses to Yoda1. These findings show that Piezo1-associated signalling is shaped over minutes by force magnitude, recent mechanical history and actin-sensitive mechanical coupling, providing a quantitative framework for understanding mechanotransduction under sustained and repeated mechanical stimulation.
n872dbeb7c5d1: Rather than being static, proteins adopt multiple conformations and undergo dynamics on a wide range of timescales. Such conformational changes can be routinely probed by solution state NMR for protein sizes below 40 kDa and can be extended to large protein complexes with selective methyl-labeling strategies. Here, we expand the limit of methyl-NMR dynamics experiments to asymmetric protein complexes bigger than 300 kDa by investigating the inert core of the eukaryotic RNA exosome, Exo9. We demonstrate that isolated subunits are highly dynamic on the ms-s dynamics, which facilitates assembly. While ring subunits lose dynamics upon complex-formation, cap subunits and functional loops retain a large degree of flexibility as demonstrated by relaxation dispersion and chemical exchange saturation transfer experiments in the fully asymmetric Exo9 complex. Employing EPR spectroscopy we additionally revealed changes in the conformational ensemble and nanosecond dynamics of a spin-labeled functional loop region in the presence of the catalytic subunit Rrp44 and in response to substrate RNA binding. We thus demonstrate that an integrated NMR-EPR approach facilitates the characterization of functional dynamics that occur on a wide range of timescales in very large protein complexes.
n0dd4229f8935: The peptidoglycan (PG) cell wall protects bacteria from osmotic lysis and determines their shape. In rod-shaped bacteria, the lateral wall is elongated by the Rod system (elongasome). This synthetic machine is built around the RodA-PBP2 PG synthase complex, the actin-like protein MreB, and the accessory proteins MreC, MreD, and RodZ. Notably, RodZ shares a similar domain organization with FtsN, an essential division protein that triggers PG synthesis by the division apparatus (divisome). Both are single pass transmembrane proteins that bind actin-like proteins in the cytoplasm and have largely unstructured periplasmic regions capped by small, folded C-terminal domains. We therefore investigated whether RodZ might function like FtsN in activating the Rod system. To this end, gain-of-function variants of Escherichia coli RodZ were isolated that restored growth and shape to cells producing a hypomorphic mreC mutant. Production of these RodZ variants in wild-type cells increased resistance to the MreB antagonist A22 and enhanced sensitivity to the beta-lactam mecillinam. These phenotypes have all previously been associated with Rod system hyperactivation, and we found that they were caused by substitutions in the cytoplasmic juxtamembrane (JM) domain of RodZ. This domain is analogous to the N-terminus of FtsN known to promote divisome activation via its interaction with filaments of the actin-like FtsA protein. Structural modeling indicates that the JM domain of RodZ is similarly likely to associate with MreB filaments. Our results therefore support a model in which RodZ activates PG synthesis by the Rod system via a mechanism analogous to divisome activation by FtsN.
n2c569a11bb0b: Glyphosate (GLY), the active ingredient in Roundup, is a broad-spectrum herbicide widely used in commercial agriculture and residential landscaping. Due to its extensive application and high water solubility, GLY is frequently introduced into freshwater ecosystems where it has been shown to negatively impact aquatic life and beneficial microorganisms. The freshwater clam Corbicula fluminea, a nonnative bivalve species widely distributed throughout the United States, is highly tolerant of many environmental stressors and may serve as a reservoir for microbial taxa capable of tolerating or degrading environmental pollutants. As efficient filter-feeders, these clams are continuously exposed to waterborne contaminants, potentially facilitating interactions between pollutants and host-associated microbial communities. In this study, we investigated how glyphosate impacts the structure and diversity of Corbicula fluminea microbiomes and characterized GLY tolerance and degradation potential in individual microbiome members. We found that microbiome taxonomic composition and abundance-based diversity metrics were minimally impacted by glyphosate, while presence/absence-based phylogenetic diversity shifted depending on treatment concentration. Furthermore, high GLY concentrations were linked to reduced Faith''s PD alpha diversity, while other alpha diversity metrics were not impacted. Additionally, we isolated and characterized glyphosate-tolerant bacterial strains from clam tissues and assessed their presence within the microbiome. Several isolates exhibited tolerance to very high GLY levels (up to 1600 mg/L), and several also utilized GLY as a sole phosphorus source and possessed the phnJ gene, suggesting potential degradation capabilities. While isolated bacteria were minority members of the microbiome, more abundant uncultured taxa were phylogenetically related to known glyphosate degraders. Collectively, these findings suggest that freshwater bivalves may harbor diverse microbial taxa capable of tolerating or degrading herbicides, which may contribute to host resilience in contaminated freshwater environments and potentially represent unexplored avenues for bioremediation research.
n2157f5255db4: Xenograft sorting tools separate sequenced DNA reads by species. We have enhanced the computational method and tool Xengsort to enable efficient epigenetic profiling of patient-derived xenograft models; it now supports cytosine-converted whole genome or reduced-representation data. Benchmarking Xengsort against several established methods (ICRG, bamcmp, XenofilteR) revealed consistently high accuracy across tools, but Xengsort outperformed the other tools in computational efficiency due to its alignment-free design.
n7610b6ac2c31: Extinct and unsampled species vastly outnumber the species typically included in phylogenetic studies. Most of these so-called ``ghost lineages'' are unknown and, among them, those that are extinct may have left no trace in the fossil record. Horizontal gene transfers (HGTs), however, provide a potential source of information about these missing lineages, because transfers can connect sampled ancestral species to lineages outside the sampled species tree. Such transfers may leave observable signatures in gene trees. Here, we formalize this signal under idealized models of duplication, transfer, and loss, and characterize the information that can be retrieved about the complete species tree (containing ghost and non-ghost lineages) thanks to sampled gene trees and sampled species trees (containing only the non-ghost lineages). We establish four identifiability results, assuming an infinite number of gene families and errorless dated gene trees. First, transfers identify the lineage through time (LTT) curve of the complete tree, averaged over each time interval induced by the nodes of the sampled species tree. Second, in the presence of transfers, the distribution of node heights in sampled gene trees uniquely determines the internal speciation times of the complete species tree, including ghost speciations. Third, these hidden speciation times suffice to restore identifiability of birth-death-sampling parameters, through a reduction to a recent theorem of Dieselhorst and Stadler. Finally, when duplication, transfer, and loss rates are known constants and the transfer rate is non-zero, the distribution of sampled gene trees almost surely uniquely determines the topology and branch lengths of the complete species tree, including all ghost branches. These results provide a theoretical basis for using signatures left by HGTs in gene trees to recover information about extinct and unsampled lineages, and suggest ways in which this signal could be exploited in practice.
n8934d6d0426a: The development of biological engineering tools have improved the ability to embed novel functions into living organisms. Concurrently, our understanding of the interface between synthetic genetic circuits and their host has accelerated in the past decade, enabling the development of context-aware predictive models. However, long-term circuit function remains difficult to predict when designs operate in field-relevant conditions. Specifically, while synthetic genetic circuits are typically characterized during exponential growth, these must operate for extended periods of time in nutrient-limited conditions and where bacteria enter stationary growth phase. In this work, we construct a mathematical model that captures the dynamics of a genetic circuit as cells transition into stationary growth phase. To achieve this, we construct synthetic genetic circuits with fluorescent reporter output and measure plasmid DNA copy number, mRNA level, protein level, and live cell count over the course of one week in stationary growth phase. We find that transcription rates plummet shortly after entering stationary phase but settle at a basal value that depends on both the promoter and ribosome binding site. Translation rates also decline in stationary phase, but protein accumulation due to lack of cell division can increase protein levels well beyond exponential phase. Our model recapitulates these findings and is capable of predicting the output of new genetic circuits. This model can serve as a tool to determine how a genetic circuit design may change on longer time scales where cells enter stationary growth phase.
na45ebc01badc: Catalytic metal-binding sites are established drug targets for many human diseases, yet systematic study of how metal function relates to disease is limited by the lack of a resource combining structural localization of human metal-binding sites with catalytic annotation at scale. We introduce HEAM (the Human Enzymatic Annotation of Metalloproteins), a structurally annotated dataset of 1,933 human metalloenzymes and 1,171 non-catalytic metalloproteins. HEAM incorporates annotated metals into protein structures at their corresponding binding sites and classifies each site as catalytic or non-catalytic using the machine learning classifier MAHOMES II. HEAM more than quadruples the human site-level coverage of the largest prior metalloenzyme database. Using HEAM, we show that human metalloproteins are significantly enriched in KEGG disease pathways relative to the human proteome, and that metalloenzymes specifically are significantly enriched in ClinVar pathogenic variants -- a distinction obscured in prior, catalytically unresolved metalloprotein datasets. These pathogenic variants are concentrated in metabolic disorders, indicating that metabolic dysfunction is a substantial contributor to metalloenzyme-linked disease. By pairing 3D structural annotation with catalytic classification, HEAM provides both a foundation for structure-guided drug design against metal-binding sites and a resource for determining how catalytic and non-catalytic metal function contribute to human disease.
n2563ddc66cea: Cell assemblies--groups of neurons that fire synchronously--are central to neuronal computation. Technological advances now permit the simultaneous recording of large neuronal populations; however, many existing cell assembly detection algorithms rely on simplified measures such as pairwise correlations, failing to capture higher-order synchrony and thereby missing a rich repertoire of assemblies present in the data. To address these limitations, we developed Identification of Synchronously Active Cells (ISAC), which performs a rigorous, iterative search across all recorded units, leveraging the full dimensionality of the dataset to detect groups that fire together above chance. Using simulated recordings with ground-truth assemblies of increasing complexity, we demonstrate that ISAC considerably outperforms currently used algorithms in identifying synchronously active cells. Finally, we show that applying ISAC to experimental recordings uncovers novel features of assembly formation and dynamics. The power and sensitivity of ISAC can thus enable insights that remain inaccessible with existing methods. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.
na42a96565824: Background: Cachexia is a frequent complication of advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD), i.e. renal cachexia, particularly in patients undergoing hemodialysis in whom it represents one of the strongest predictors of morbidity and mortality. Yet, our understanding of the molecular mechanisms leading to body wasting in CKD and management of cachectic patients are still poorly defined. To date, a preclinical mouse model of robust and reproducible CKD-associated cachexia is missing. Here, we assessed in a systematic manner the cachectic phenotype of the genetic Col4a3-/- mouse model of CKD. Methods: 129/SvJ Col4a3-/- male and female animals were monitored longitudinally until they developed kidney failure. Measured glomerular filtration rate (mGFR), body composition and grip strength were recorded at baseline (6 weeks of age, before onset of kidney dysfunction) and at endpoint (CKD with weight loss or 12 weeks of age). The severity of CKD was confirmed by biochemical and histological analyses. Muscle atrophy was assessed via fiber cross-sectional area analysis, atrogene expression and transcriptomics. Adipose tissue wasting was assessed by measuring adipocyte area and proteins involved in lipid synthesis and breakdown. Liver acute phase response and systemic inflammation were evaluated by measuring circulating levels of key factors using ELISA. Results: Col4a3-/- animals developed CKD (decrease in mGFR: -85%, P<0.0001) and cachexia within 8-12 weeks of age. Cachexia was characterized by a progressive loss of body weight (-17.8% +/- 1.0, P<0.0001), lean (-8.2% +/- 2.0, P<0.0001) and fat mass (-66.5% +/- 4.7, P<0.0001) associated with reduced grip strength (-24.3% +/- 0.0, P=0.0002). At the tissue level, cachexia led to muscle atrophy and induction of atrogenes. Muscle transcriptomics further validated the cachectic phenotype of the Col4a3-/-, with 47% of genes altered in a similar manner with the well-established colon-C26 mouse model of cancer cachexia. It also revealed signatures that appeared more specific to renal cachexia. Adipose tissue wasting was characterized by a depletion in fat stores, consecutive to an imbalance between proteins involved in lipogenesis and lipolysis. Cachexia in this model was also associated with the induction of acute phase response in liver, elevated circulating levels of serum amyloid A and systemic inflammation, with the induction of established cachexia mediators (IL-6, GDF-15 P<0.0001). Both male and female mice developed cachexia. Conclusions: Our data highlight the potential of using the Col4a3-/- mouse model of CKD for the future study of renal cachexia, offering a more robust alternative to classically used models of partial nephrectomy or adenine-rich diet.
n3839e5b561df: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) are central regulators of gene expression. In bacteria, two KH domain-containing proteins, KhpA and KhpB, are increasingly recognized as globally-acting RBPs, including in pathogens that lack well-studied RBPs, such as Hfq and ProQ. While KhpA and KhpB interact with various RNAs in diverse bacteria, their crosstalk and molecular basis of RNA recognition remain poorly understood. Here, we explored the mutual dependence between KhpA and KhpB in the food-borne pathogen Campylobacter jejuni . We demonstrate KhpA and KhpB interact in vivo , and their individual global RNA recognition is largely dependent on the presence of the partner protein. Using RNA co-immunoprecipitation, we reveal that KhpA requires a conserved KH domain motif for RNA binding, whereas KhpB relies on an atypical R3H domain. Moreover, mutating the RNA-binding domain of one protein compromises the RNA interactome of the other. Overall, we demonstrate an interdependent RNA-binding mode of KhpA and KhpB and anticipate that such KH-proteins have co-evolved to elicit joint RNA regulation in bacteria.
n4ffbc40b2154: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) triggers persistent neuroimmune and neurovascular dysfunction that contributes to secondary brain injury and limits recovery. Here, we investigated whether a single intranasal dose of LMNSC01 could reprogram neuroinflammatory and neurovascular responses post TBI and whether these effects were conserved across biological sex. Immunocompetent male and female rats underwent a controlled cortical impact (CCI) or Sham surgery and 7 days later received a single bolus dose of LMNSC01 (6 x10^6 cells/dose) or vehicle. Integrated histological and transcriptomic analyses and multiplex tissue ELISA were used to characterize injury- and treatment-associated responses. CCI induced persistent but sex-dependent transcriptional changes. Male rats exhibited prominent innate immune, adhesion, extracellular matrix, and tissue remodeling responses, whereas females demonstrated broader activation of microglial, interferon, complement, MHC/antigen presentation, and humoral/adaptive immune pathways. LMNSC01 treatment reprogrammed these distinct injury states through partially sex-specific mechanisms. In males, LMNSC01 increased endogenous immune-regulatory mediators, including Il1rn, and reduced pathways associated with adhesion and immune cell trafficking. In females, treatment decreased expression of genes related to microglial, leukocyte, MHC/antigen presentation, cytokine, and adhesion pathways, and reduced macrophage- and CD45 positive cell signatures. Despite these sex-dependent transcriptional changes, LMNSC01 produced conserved protein changes in both sexes, reducing injury associated ICAM-1 and restoring CX3CL1 proteins, proposing a novel molecular mechanism of LMNSCs modulating endothelial activation and neuron-microglia communication post injury. Our study provides further insight into sex differences in responses to injury and treatment after TBI and highlights candidate repair mechanisms, supporting further development of LMNSC01 as a minimally invasive therapy for TBI.
n8619d0ada1ca: Many pathogens spend a substantial portion of their life cycle outside the host tissues. During its free-living stage, the root legume-plant pathogen Aphanomyces euteiches persists in soil either as non-motile resting oospores or actively explores the environment through mycelium and motile zoospores. These two latter stages are critical for survival, dispersal and host encounter. However, the extent of intraspecific variation during these phases remains poorly explored, and it is still unknown whether they are organized into phenotypic syndromes contributing to infection success. Here, we measured eight free-living phenotypic traits associated with mycelial and zoospore stages across 23 A. euteiches strains from distinct geographic regions (USA, Europe) whose genomes were sequenced. We tested whether traits are organized into a phenotypic syndrome linked to either geographic origin, genomic diversity or infectivity. The microbial strains exhibited substantial intraspecific phenotypic variation that we proposed as an 'exploration syndrome' linked to host search. Beyond this general syndrome, we detected sub-structure according to strains' infectivity, geographic origin and genetic group. This suggests that the free-living stage of pathogens may contribute to disease potential. Our results highlight the importance of integrating functional trait approaches into plant pathology and suggest that the identified "exploration syndrome" may serve as a predictor of infectivity in soilborne oomycete pathogens.
n3189610d3bd3: An experimental study of myosin I motors on a supported lipid membrane with a nematic actin filament layer is presented. The activities of myosin I motors re-organize the actin layer, in particular the morphology of +1/2 nematic defects. Data from single-particle tracking (SPT) of lipid molecules reveal two interesting features. First, the distribution of average lipid speed over a track shows two groups of lipids (high-speed and low-speed), and the proportion of lipids to be high-speed is higher in regions rich in actin. Second, by classifying short-time movement of the lipids into normal diffusion, directed motion, confined motion, and subdiffusion states, we found that lipids in regions rich in actin have a lower probability to stay in the confined and subdiffusion states and more likely to perform normal diffusion. Furthermore, fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) measurements show that the diffusion of lipids in the actin-rich regions is enhanced. The SPT and FRAP results suggest that myosin I motor activities turn low-speed lipids to high-speed ones, and affect the lipid moving state by reducing confined and subdiffusive motion. As a result, lipid diffusion is enhanced by motor activities.
nbaacf830094f: Enzymes that cleave the bacterial peptidoglycan sacculus, known collectively as autolysins, are critical for growth, division and morphogenesis, but their activities must be carefully controlled to avoid catastrophic lysis. Some autolysin control mechanisms have emerged, but we still know little about how most of them are regulated. Here, we report a novel control mechanism for the LytM/M23 family endopeptidase PA4404 in P. aeruginosa, which we have named LmdC. We have discovered that LmdC is auto catalytically cleaved into N- and C-terminal domains that are then degraded by the carboxyl-terminal processing proteases Prc and CtpA respectively. The effects of various mutations on LmdC-linked {beta}-lactam resistance suggested that full length LmdC is the functional enzyme, with its auto catalytic cleavage serving only to initiate its proteolytic destruction. The auto catalytic cleavage of LmdC was inhibited by overproducing a polymer-forming cytoskeletal protein bactofilin homolog encoded by PA0664, which we named Baf, and a protein of unknown function encoded by PA0663, which we named Api (auto processing inhibitor). We hypothesize that Baf and Api could promote a location specific role for LmdC. In this scenario, the dangerous potential for any free LmdC to cleave peptidoglycan at the wrong place would be prevented by its immediate auto processing and degradation. The widespread co-occurrence and linkage of lmdC and baf homologs, coupled with conserved features of those LmdC homologs, makes it likely that regulated LmdC auto processing is a widely conserved control mechanism.
nccb91cc118d0: Partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (pEMT) was defined in single malignant cells of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma but is usually scored in bulk tumours. In three single-cell datasets, its laminin-332 and hemidesmosome genes were expressed by malignant cells (the malignant arm) and its fibrillar collagens and vimentin by fibroblasts (the stromal arm). In bulk tumours the stromal arm dominated co-expression, so standard pEMT scores mainly measure stroma. We recovered the malignant arm with a classifier trained on single cells and a 12-gene core. In 40 patients treated with platinum and cetuximab, both malignant measures were higher in those with long progression-free survival (area under the curve 0.78 and 0.82), and the stromal arm was not. The malignant arm was inseparable from the Basal subtype, whose score did as well or better in these patients (0.93) and in two xenograft panels. Bulk pEMT scores should be read by cell of origin.
