n9c69216170e9: Shotgun metagenomics routinely resolves microbial community composition down to the strain level via metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), but translating these static catalogs into mechanistic, time-resolved understandings of ecosystem dynamics remains a critical computational bottleneck. Here, we present muODE, a fully automated framework that converts MAGs into dynamical simulations of community metabolism equipped with a composable, literature-grounded ecology layer, fundamentally designed to serve as a mechanistic hypothesis-testing engine. It employs dynamic flux balance analysis (dFBA) coupled to a shared extracellular pool and integrates a composable ecology layer capturing pH inhibition, time-varying antibiotic pharmacokinetics, bile-acid transformations, and spore dormancy. To evaluate the core engine, we cross-validated the dFBA machinery to machine precision against an independent reference implementation. We provide native export to the established COMETS engine for third-party verification. Benchmarking against two independent experimentally validated datasets confirmed that while monoculture growth is robustly captured, overflow secretion and directed community composition remain strictly bounded by the flux-routing limitations of max-biomass FBA. However, when applied to rate-modifying ecological feedback, muODE mechanistically and quantitatively reproduces bile-acid-mediated colonization resistance against Clostridioides difficile. With a single rate parameter calibrated so that baseline deoxycholate matched its measured physiological concentration, the framework reproduced the uncalibrated antibiotic-induced collapse of deoxycholate, with the calibrated inhibitor concentration coinciding with the independently set inhibitory threshold of the pathogen and driving a ~44x shift in the simulated pathogen-susceptibility ratio; bile-acid transformation is represented in the composable ecology layer rather than in the genome-scale stoichiometry. Finally, applying muODE end-to-end to a real longitudinal fecal microbiota transplant (FMT) yielding 139 de novo genome-scale metabolic models, the framework successfully recovered the clinical direction of treatment. By transparently diagnosing the structural competitive-exclusion bias that limits precise compositional prediction, muODE motivates the necessity of community-objective extensions while transitioning microbiome modeling from descriptive taxonomy toward testable, quantitatively-validated dynamic hypothesis testing, laying the essential mechanistic groundwork for the predictive engineering of safe, targeted ecological therapeutics. muODE is freely available at https://github.com/cumbof/muODE.
n9e7166842e75: Background: Heart failure (HF) is a major public health challenge in ageing populations and a leading cause of unplanned hospital readmissions. Biological, social, and economic factors contribute to recurrent hospitalisation, but gaps remain in understanding how these factors interact and patterns of healthcare use following hospitalisation. Methods: We conducted an explanatory sequential mixed-methods study of patients aged ?60 years with an HF hospital admission between 2016 and 2020 who completed the Sax Institute?s 45 and Up Study baseline questionnaire. Data were linked to Admitted Patient Data Collection, Medicare Benefits Schedule, and Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme data. HF readmission within 30 days of the index admission was the outcome. Cox proportional hazards models estimated crude and adjusted hazard ratios (HRs and adjHRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests compared survival between groups. Time-series plots mapped healthcare interactions over 1 year following the index admission. Results: Among 4,252 patients with HF, 409 were readmitted within 30 days. Significant predictors included age ?80 years (adjHR, 1.30; 95%CI, 1.01?1.67), 1 chronic condition (adjHR, 2.49; 95%CI, 1.41?4.40), ?2 chronic conditions (adjHR, 1.75; 95%CI, 1.04?2.95), and alcohol consumption above national guidelines (adjHR, 1.45; 95%CI, 1.06?1.98). Time-series analysis indicated that participants with readmission had more frequent out-of-hospital health service contact following their initial HF admission than those without readmission. Conclusions: Older age, chronic conditions, and high alcohol intake increased 30-day HF readmission risk. Differences in healthcare use after admission highlight opportunities for targeted and coordinated post-discharge care.
nac7b893d1e72: Purpose: Post-marketing reports have associated faricimab, the first intravitreal bispecific antibody, with intraocular inflammation (IOI). Its inflammatory phenotype, temporal pattern and systemic safety relative to established anti-VEGF agents remain unclear. We compared faricimab, aflibercept and ranibizumab across three independent pharmacovigilance databases. Methods: We analysed FAERS reports from Q1 2022 to Q2 2026, with external validation in JADER (PMDA, Japan) and EudraVigilance. Reports were de-duplicated, restricted to primary-suspect reports, and a pre-specified list of 36 non-adverse-event preferred terms (PTs) was excluded. We computed reporting odds ratios (ROR), proportional reporting ratios and Bayesian information components, with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate control. Head-to-head RORs were adjusted for demographic confounders by logistic regression. Time to onset (TTO) was modelled with Weibull distributions. Sensitivity analyses addressed masking and differential market duration. Signals were graded with a pre-specified bidirectional cross-database evidence framework (Confirmed, Consistent, Unconfirmed, Discordant). Results: Faricimab was reported more often for anterior-chamber and vitreal inflammation. Adjusted RORs (comparator versus faricimab, values <1 indicating faricimab excess) were 0.27 (95% CI 0.18-0.40) for iridocyclitis and 0.45 (0.35-0.58) for uveitis versus aflibercept, and 0.13 (0.06-0.24) and 0.12 (0.06-0.20) versus ranibizumab. All four PTs were Confirmed in JADER against both comparators; for iridocyclitis, RORs were 0.048 versus aflibercept and 0.109 versus ranibizumab. Faricimab IOI arose late (median TTO 100 days, IQR 31-182, versus 7 days for both comparators; P = 2.6E-14) and its Weibull onset distribution was markedly flatter (shape 0.81 versus {approx}0.42). In contrast, aflibercept predominated for endophthalmitis-spectrum events and intraocular pressure elevation, and ranibizumab for vitreous haemorrhage, the latter confirmed in JADER. Faricimab showed lower reporting across cardiac, nervous system, vascular and renal system organ classes, confirmed in EudraVigilance. An unadjusted FAERS death signal (ROR 3.16, aflibercept versus faricimab) attenuated after adjustment (aROR {approx}1.8) and was absent in outcome-based JADER analyses. Conclusions: Faricimab exhibits a reproducible, delayed-onset, anterior-predominant IOI phenotype alongside a comparatively favourable systemic safety profile. Clinicians should be aware that faricimab-associated IOI may arise weeks to months after injection. Prospective studies with exposure denominators are needed to quantify absolute risk.
n95d0d027daca: Background: Patients increasingly consult free artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots about their symptoms, but these models may favour agreement with the patient over accuracy. In obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), where most cases in the general population remain undiagnosed and diagnosis depends on referral, this could validate symptom denial. We tested whether consumer chatbots maintain guideline-concordant referral when a simulated patient minimises symptoms. Methods: Seven guideline-concordant and standardised OSA vignettes (apnoea-hypopnoea-index, AHI 8-52 events/h; body mass index 28-42 kg/m2) were presented to five free chatbots (GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude Sonnet 4.6, DeepSeek V4 Flash and Grok-4.3) under neutral and symptom-minimising conditions (10 simulated conversations per model-vignette-condition cell; N=700). Referral maintenance was scored by a structured rubric and every capitulation was human-confirmed. Results: All chatbots maintained referral recommendations in neutral conversations (350/350; 100%). When simulated patients minimised symptoms and resisted referral, maintenance fell to 64.3% (225/350), a reduction of 35.7 percentage points (95% CI 5.5-66.0; p=0.028). Rates ranged from 55.7% to 85.7% across chatbots, but evidence of between-chatbot differences was inconsistent across analyses. Rates differed across clinical vignettes (p=0.001). A variance analysis estimated greater variation between vignettes than between chatbots. In the three driving-risk vignettes, referral recommendations were abandoned in 46-68% of symptom-minimising conversations, pooling all five chatbots within each vignette. Conclusions: Consumer AI chatbots abandoned correct OSA referral recommendations in about one-third of symptom-minimising conversations, with higher observed abandonment in simulated cases involving driving risk. This may delay appropriate assessment and raises patient- and public-safety concerns.
na158d304aa2f: Background Patients with normal perfusion, normal myocardial flow reserve (MFR) and no coronary artery calcium (CAC) on myocardial perfusion imaging are considered low risk. Yet, adverse events still occur and no routinely reported imaging marker stratifies residual risk. This study aims to determine whether fully automated ascending aortic calcification (AAC) from the attenuation correction CT stratifies risk in these patients. Methods In the multicenter REFINE-PET registry, AAC was quantified from non-contrast CT using deep learning aortic segmentation and Agatston scoring. Triple-normal was defined as stress total perfusion deficit (TPD) 2 and CAC 0. The primary endpoint was cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or heart failure admission, with heart failure admission as key secondary endpoint. Cox models were adjusted for clinical confounders. Results Of 21,923 patients, 3,580 (16.3%) were triple-normal, of whom 1,322 (36.9%) had AAC (median Agatston 65, IQR 22-212). Agreement with three blinded readers was good to excellent (Intraclass correlation coefficient 0.87-0.90). Over a median follow-up of 52 months (IQR 26-69), 194 primary events occurred. Per standard deviation, AAC was independently associated with the primary endpoint (adjusted HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.09-1.40; p<0.001), heart failure admission (adjusted HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.10-1.55; p=0.003) and all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 1.17, 95% CI 1.04-1.32; p=0.009). AAC improved model fit beyond clinical factors, MFR and TPD (p< or =0.009), with modest gains in discrimination ({Delta}C 0.007-0.009). Conclusions In patients with normal PET readouts, automated AAC was independently associated with adverse outcomes, most strongly heart failure admission, beyond clinical risk factors, perfusion and flow.
n191711f7776c: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) may involve impaired dynamic regulation of brain states that is not captured by conventional resting-state electroencephalography (EEG). We quantified occipital alpha (8-12 Hz) transitions during three repeated eye-opening/eye-closure cycles in 60 healthy controls (HC) and 77 participants with MCI. Eye-state events were refined from frontal ocular artifacts. Transition magnitude was measured by the log-transformed post-/pre-event energy ratio, and transition success by the expected direction of alpha change. For canonical transitions meeting prespecified fit-quality criteria, mono-exponential fitting yielded transition onset (t_onset) and the post-onset time constant (tau). MCI showed weaker alpha suppression during eye opening, weaker alpha enhancement during eye closure, and lower odds of transition success. No significant group difference in tau was detected within the canonical quality-controlled subset. In contrast, t_onset showed significant Group x Trial interactions in both conditions: HC developed later onset during eye opening and earlier onset during eye closure across repetitions, whereas MCI showed no comparable change. These findings suggest reduced alpha state-transition capacity and altered repetition-dependent temporal organization in MCI.
nf0352f906b5c: Objective Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate, summarize, and evaluate clinical documentation, yet standardized methods for evaluating nuanced, context-dependent clinical language remain limited. Existing approaches rely primarily on annotated clinical corpora or keyword-based methods, restricting reproducibility, public dissemination, and systematic comparison across models. We present ClinStigma, a clinician-guided framework for constructing, annotating, and evaluating synthetic benchmarks of contextual stigmatizing language, demonstrated through ClinStigma-SUD, its inaugural implementation for substance use disorder documentation. Materials and Methods Candidate clinical sentences were generated using a frontier language model and iteratively reviewed according to a clinician-developed annotation rubric refined through expert review in stigmatizing language. The resulting benchmark intentionally incorporates explicit stigmatizing, neutral, and contextually ambiguous ("gray-zone") documentation requiring clinical reasoning rather than keyword recognition. Three locally deployed open-weight LLMs were evaluated using zero-shot inference, followed by external evaluation using independently annotated clinical documentation from MIMIC-IV. Results ClinStigma-SUD consists of 500 clinician-adjudicated synthetic clinical documentation sentences. Inter-rater agreement was 98.8% across the full benchmark (Cohen's {kappa} = 0.976) and 94.0% within the intentionally ambiguous subset ({kappa} = 0.880). Under zero-shot prompting, binary accuracy ranged from 84.8% to 91.8% across evaluated models, while F1 for the ambiguous (gray) class ranged from 0.038 to 0.423. Zero-shot external evaluation on 3,716 annotated examples from the independently annotated Harrigian MIMIC-IV corpus yielded 84.4% accuracy (84.4% balanced accuracy; macro F1 0.824), against a 69.9% majority-class baseline. Stigmatizing-class F1 was 0.879 in the substance-related subgroup and 0.883 in the full external corpus. Discussion and Conclusion ClinStigma establishes a reproducible clinician-guided framework for developing synthetic evaluation benchmarks for contextual clinical language. By combining structured clinical expertise, explicit annotation guidance, synthetic benchmark generation, and external evaluation, the framework enables open, privacy-preserving evaluation of language models while providing a scalable foundation for benchmark development across additional clinical specialties, including obstetrics, emergency medicine, and mental health.
n587a30478a02: Modern clinical medicine depends on reducing complex human realities into forms that support knowledge, judgment, and action. Such reduction is indispensable to scientific medicine, but necessarily selective. A medical framing may therefore remain well warranted within medicine while becoming insufficient in relation to the reality of a particular patient. What happens clinically when the adequacy of such a framing itself becomes uncertain remains insufficiently understood. We conducted an abductive, theory-generating qualitative study of 44 patients who attended a supplementary Dialogue-Based Outpatient Clinic within a breast oncology service in Japan between 2021 and 2023, comprising 111 consultations. The clinic had no predefined clinical agenda, allowing patients to raise concerns that mattered to them. Through iterative comparison within and across cases, we examined how patients' concerns were understood and responded to clinically. Across cases, a recurrent clinical process became apparent when patient reality called the adequacy of existing medical framing into question. Exploration of patients' concerns could expose a consequential mismatch between their reality and the framing through which medicine understands and represents clinical reality. Such mismatches prompted inquiry into medical framing to identify what required reopening. Reopening occurred when the identified framing, previously treated as provisionally settled, became reconsiderable in relation to the patient's reality. Reconsideration involved examining what had been reopened and exploring clinical responses through dialogue between clinician and patient, followed by a clinical response and provisional closure. We describe this recurrent process as Clinical Epistemic Reopening (CER). CER identifies a clinical process through which the framing produced by medicine's necessary selectivity in making complex reality clinically knowable and actionable can itself become reconsiderable when patient reality reveals its limits. CER can thereby reverse the usual direction of clinical scrutiny: aspects of medicine that ordinarily function as means of understanding and acting upon the patient can themselves become objects of clinical inquiry. CER thus allows medicine to remain open to patient reality beyond the limits of its existing framings.
n2abb72c8c0f0: Human centromeres harbor extensive structural variation that has remained largely inaccessible to human genetics because their repetitive -satellite arrays are absent from standard reference and imputation panels. Here we catalog 188,589 centromeric structural variants (SVs) from haplotype-resolved long-read assemblies of 196 Human Pangenome Reference Consortium individuals aligned to the telomere-to-telomere CHM13 reference. Resolving recurrent SVs into monophyletic components along centromeric haplotype phylogenies makes them imputable from pericentromeric SNPs (mean R2CV = 0.407 vs. 0.065 unresolved). In 124 individuals with haplotype-resolved nanopore methylation, we identify 418 same-chromosome SV-CpG associations that form local hypomethylation-enriched domains in the centromeric region, most strongly for deletions. We also show that a truncated 113-bp monomer on chromosome 8 is associated with the position of the CENP-A-associated centromere dip region (CDR) at n = 151, independent of array length. Imputed into 630 individuals with expression and splicing data, centromeric SVs are associated with 141 genes, 14 of them new relative to the SNP-based cis-QTL analysis, including the H3K9 methyltransferase SUV39H1. In 315,204 All of Us participants, we identify 170 associations between 61 SV predictors and 27 clinical phenotypes, including substance-related disorders and breast cancer. Our study brings a previously inaccessible class of variation into population-scale genetics and links centromeric SVs to centromere organization, gene expression, splicing and complex traits.
n5dc87937755c: Importance. Suicide is a leading cause of mortality, yet its prevention remains a challenge. Suicide attempters exhibit disrupted decision-making, but the specific cognitive processes driving this impairment and their utility for risk stratification are unclear. Objective. To determine which computational decision-making mechanisms are disrupted in high-risk suicide attempters, and whether they distinguish attempters from depressed and healthy controls. Design. This cross-sectional study fit reinforcement-learning models to Iowa Gambling Task performance across two independent studies: SPAD (August 2017 to May 2020); SUICIDE-DECIDE (March 2021 to September 2023). Data was analyzed between January 2025 and July 2026. Setting. SPAD was conducted in Nimes (France). SUICIDE-DECIDE was a muticenter study across Jena (Germany) and Nimes. Clinical groups were recruited from academic inpatient psychiatry units and outpatient clinics, and healthy controls through local advertisement. Participants. SPAD included adults aged 60 years or older; SUICIDE-DECIDE middle-aged adults stratified by attempt means (violent/nonviolent). Consecutive participants were recruited into three groups: suicide attempters, patient controls, healthy controls. Main outcomes and measures. The primary outcomes were group differences on parameters reflecting learning from rewards and losses, sensitivity to win frequency, choice perseverance, and forgetting of past choices. We trained a multinomial logistic regression model in the SUICIDE-DECIDE study using self-reported depression and parameters that differentiated attempters from controls across studies, and evaluated its performance in the SPAD sample. Results. SPAD included 57 participants (40 females [70.2%]; mean [SD] age, 70.1 [8.2]). SUICIDE-DECIDE included 124 participants (77 females [62.1%]; 32.1 [11.0]). Suicide attempters forgot past choices faster than controls (SPAD: F(2,36) = 13.5; P < .001; SUICIDE-DECIDE: F(3,57) = 46.6; P < .001). No other parameter specifically differed in attempters across studies. In SUICIDE-DECIDE, greater forgetting of past choices was associated with attempter status only (RRR = 4.2, 95% CI [1.5, 11.5]). This parameter paired with depression severity correctly classified 87.2% of participants in SPAD (95% CI [74.3%, 95.2%], 41/47). Conclusions and relevance. Short-sighted decision-making may represent a cognitive phenotype associated with suicide in high-risk populations and a potential target for prevention and treatment.
nb1a4dfe0c35c: Decision models like Jev read text and return probabilities, categories, or ordinal levels, with confidence scores for the latter two, at a fraction of large language models' (LLMs) cost. We explored how Jev could be integrated into clinical workflows for all these output types: mortality risk estimation, categorical Choosing-Wisely decisions for patient questions, and ordinal colon cancer staging. With standard LLM-style inputs, Jev trailed five flagship LLMs: mortality AUROC was 0.822 versus 0.837-0.846; Choosing-Wisely accuracy, 87.7% versus 98.4-100%; and staging accuracy, 45.4% versus 94.2-100%. Developer-recommended input alterations improved staging accuracy to 75.8% with medical context, 82.1% with task decomposition, and 85.8% with both. None of Jev's staging errors had full confidence. Using Jev for fully confident staging decisions and LLMs for the rest was non-inferior to each LLM alone and cut flagship LLM costs by 33-44%. Prompted as designed, decision models may efficiently share structured clinical tasks with LLMs.
n775644931165: Background: Handgrip strength is associated with cardiometabolic abnormalities, but whether it adds information once detailed adiposity and muscle mass are known is unclear. Methods: We studied adults aged 40-59 years from NHANES 2011-2012 (development, n=508) and 2013-2014 (temporal validation, n=616). The outcome was at least two of four non-adiposity abnormalities (elevated blood pressure, fasting glucose or triglycerides, or low HDL cholesterol); waist circumference was not part of the outcome. A prespecified feature ladder added DXA body fat percentage and visceral adipose tissue to age, sex, BMI and waist circumference (M1), then appendicular skeletal muscle index (M2), then absolute (M3A, primary) or weight-normalised (M3B) grip strength. Logistic regression was primary; elastic-net and XGBoost were supportive. Development performance used nested cross-validation; frozen models were scored once in the validation cohort. Paired increments used 2000 stratified bootstrap resamples. Results: The outcome occurred in 249 (49.0%) and 277 (45.0%) participants. Adding adiposity increased the logistic regression AUC by 0.0209 (95% CI 0.0024-0.0402) in development and 0.0209 (0.0032-0.0375) in temporal validation. Adding absolute grip strength to M2 changed the AUC by -0.0046 (-0.0107 to 0.0013) and 0.0045 (-0.0009 to 0.0098), respectively. All 12 grip-strength AUC increments across algorithms, definitions and cohorts had intervals that included zero. Calibration was unchanged and the incremental net benefit was not consistently positive. Model attributions to grip strength varied by algorithm. Conclusions: In middle-aged adults, detailed adiposity, but not grip strength, added reproducible information for concurrent cardiometabolic risk stratification beyond conventional anthropometry and muscle mass.
n7cb650cb0892: The emergence of a dominant poultry-associated strain of Campylobacter jejuni in New Zealand coincided with a multi-year epidemic of human campylobacteriosis. This was characterised by an increase in cases to 2006, when one of the highest national case-rates in the world was recorded, followed by a rapid decline attributed to interventions in the poultry industry. The strain belonged to an internationally rare multilocus sequence type, ST474 - a member of Clonal Complex (CC) 48 - that was highly prevalent in both poultry and human cases in New Zealand but was also identified in other samples. ST474 isolates from humans, animal reservoirs and environmental water samples were collected between 2005 and 2019 and whole genome sequenced (N=443). Isolates from a 2018/9 case-control study of campylobacteriosis in New Zealand were included for genomic comparisons with other sequence types and CCs. This presented an opportunity to examine the genomic epidemiology of a single, relatively recently emerged lineage of C. jejuni, and improve our understanding of drivers of emergence and persistence in a relatively isolated ecosystem. Six subpopulations (clades) of ST474 were identified and these varied in terms of their host association, persistence, patterns of homologous recombination, and complement of mobile genetic elements, including plasmids and chromosomally integrated elements. Clade E was associated with a single poultry supplier in the initial epidemic phase and accounted for 34.5% of human cases. Clade F emerged from a declining Clade E after the peak in human cases and was also associated with poultry. The emergence of Clade F was accompanied by the loss of integrated element CJIE5 and the acquisition of multiple blocks of recombination, likely from diverse ancestral C. jejuni lineages, and the loss of the methionine biosynthesis operon metAB. In contrast, Clades A-D were detected at low frequencies in human cases over the 14-year period of surveillance and were associated with multiple hosts. This longitudinal study sheds light on the evolutionary processes that result in strain emergence and differentiation, highlighting the role of horizontal gene transfer in the evolution and adaptation of this pathogen to new niches, and the subsequent impact on public health.
n4f71b1338180: Cardiovascular diseases (CVD) are the leading cause of global mortality, responsible for 17.8 million deaths and 423 million prevalent cases annually. While the etiology of CVD is multifactorial, evidence confirms that multicomponent behavioral interventions regarding diet and lifestyle can substantially reduce risk. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a 12-month mHealth intervention, i.e., public health practice supported by mobile devices in reducing the 10-year CVD risk among overweight and obese adults aged 35 to 64 in an urban Sri Lankan population. A two-group parallel-arm randomized control trial (RCT) was conducted with 1,200 participants from the Colombo district, assigned either to an intervention arm (n=600) or a usual care control arm (n=600). The intervention group received automated text and voice messages in their native language at a frequency of two of each per week over 12 months. The primary outcome, 10-year CVD risk, was assessed using the WHO CVD risk prediction score. The intervention significantly reduced the proportion of participants with a 10-year CVD risk from 10.0% to 6.2% (p=0.003), whereas no significant change was observed in the control group (11.0% to 9.7%). Participants in the mHealth arm demonstrated substantial behavioral improvements, including increasing daily fruit and vegetable servings from 3.6 to 5.5 and reducing daily salt intake from 7.64g to 5.62g. Physical activity levels also improved, with 89.6% meeting minimum daily requirements compared to 77.4% at baseline. These findings suggest a potentially beneficial effect on predicted cardiovascular risk. The study concludes that an automated mHealth intervention is an effective, feasible, and acceptable approach to reducing cardiovascular risk in an urban South Asian setting. The findings provide a robust evidence base for integrating digital health strategies into national non-communicable disease (NCD) prevention policies. While the 12-month results are promising, further longitudinal research is required to evaluate the long-term sustainability of these behavioral changes and their ultimate impact on mortality rates.
nb95e5cab16c9: Background: Preventive chemotherapy via single-dose benzimidazoles remains the core strategy for soil-transmitted helminth (STH) control. However, single-dose regimens often yield sub-optimal clearance against species such as Trichuris trichiura and hookworm. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the comparative efficacy of repeated-dose versus standard single-dose albendazole or mebendazole regimens in paediatric populations. Methods: Registered prospectively on PROSPERO (CRD420261491616), a comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar identified clinical trials comparing repeated-dose against single-dose albendazole or mebendazole in paediatric STH infections. Primary outcomes were cure rate (CR) and egg reduction rate (ERR). Random-effects models synthesized pooled odds ratios (OR) and mean differences (MD). Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. Results: Five randomized clinical trials (N = 1,718 participants) met the inclusion criteria. Overall, repeated dosing demonstrated significant superiority in cure rate (pooled OR = 4.47, 95% CI: 1.58-12.67; I{superscript 2} = 92%) and egg reduction rate (pooled MD = 0.17, 95% CI: 0.01-0.32; I{superscript 2} = 87%). Discussion: Repeated-dose benzimidazole regimens offer superior overall therapeutic efficacy compared to standard single-dose administration in children. However, this therapeutic advantage is drug-specific: multi-dose albendazole consistently enhances parasite clearance across trial settings, whereas multi-dose mebendazole exhibits variable performance and lacks conclusive superiority over single dosing. Conclusion: Transitioning to targeted, multi-dose albendazole protocols--rather than mebendazole--may serve as an effective public health intervention to eliminate residual parasite reservoirs in high-transmission endemic regions.
neb61e10fcd7e: Automated surveillance systems can prove to be extremely useful in detecting outbreaks of respiratory diseases that need further epidemiological investigation. In order for the system to be effective, careful attention has to be paid to the baseline used, absence of the observations, and the use of proper statistical methods. As a solution, the paper describes EpiAlert, a weekly surveillance system based on CDC FluView ILINet. The system is able to transform the number of ILI visits and the total number of visits into a ILI prevalence for the region, create the first reference from the three previous years using a +/- 2-week interval, transform the rate value, and apply two different detectors - CUSUM and EWMA. CUSUM is set at k=0.5 and h=5, whereas EWMA uses {lambda}=0.2 and H=2.7 values. Among the 55 districts, the system gives 45,138 pieces of information about the disease by transforming 44,297 pieces of data into alerts. It is found that there are 2,820 alerts in total (out of which 2,711 alerts used CUSUM, 402 used EWMA, and 293 used both detectors). Additionally, the experiments show that the sensitivity of the device depends greatly on the detector. The latest statistics can be tracked in the report for week 37 of 2026 that recently concluded in West.
n48f2b284b2c4: Importance: The Medicare Physician Fee Schedule values ambulatory services using survey-based estimates of physician time, a costly process vulnerable to inaccuracy. EHR audit logs are passively and universally collected and likely meet the American Medical Association Relative Value Scale Update Committee (AMA RUC) Extant Database Standards for alternative data to inform service valuation estimates. However, audit logs' validity for estimating face-to-face time, a core component of many of the most used procedural codes, is unknown. Objective: To assess whether EHR audit logs can facilitate accurate estimation of physician-patient face-to-face time during ambulatory visits. Design: Single-site validation study pairing EHR audit logs with direct audio/video recordings of ambulatory primary care visits (reference standard). We assessed agreement between audit-log estimates and recorded visit duration with Bland-Altman analysis and mean absolute error. Setting: University of Pennsylvania Observer data repository, a multi-modal database of ambulatory visits to Penn Medicine primary care clinics including video and audio recordings, transcripts, clinical EHR data, and EHR audit-log data. Participants: 75 visits from 12 physicians with data collected between August 2023 and February 2025. Exposures: A rule-based algorithm estimated face-to-face time via clusters of physician EHR activity relative to patient check-in time. Inactivity thresholds were applied to differentiate intraservice time with no EHR activity (e.g., a physical exam) from the end of a visit, with longer thresholds used for longer visits. Main Outcomes and Measures: Duration of recorded face-to-face visit time. Results: Recorded face-to-face time averaged 31.6 minutes (SD, 13.9). The audit-log estimator was unbiased (mean bias: -0.63 minutes; 95% CI: -6.0 to 2.6; mean absolute error: 9.0 minutes) and estimated face-to-face time within approximately 2% (38 seconds) of the recorded visit time with no proportional bias (slope: 0.13; P = .25). The 95% limits of agreement were -25.7 to 24.4 minutes, and 37% of estimates fell within 10% of recorded duration. Conclusions and Relevance: In this validation study, EHR audit logs recovered unbiased estimates of ambulatory face-to-face time. Larger-scale studies are required to verify generalizability, but EHR audit logs offer a scalable means to improve the rigor of retrospective physician work relative value unit estimation. This study represents a first step in a potential paradigm shift for measuring components of the fee schedule across procedures, settings, and provider types.
ned60b8a48210: The FORESEE trial (NCT04450706) was a prospective study to evaluate the feasibility of integrating organoid-based drug testing with comprehensive genomic characterization to inform treatment selection in patients with HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer. The primary objective of the study was to determine the feasibility of providing personalized therapy recommendations using a combination of genomic vulnerability information with drug testing in patient-derived organoids (PDOs) in a clinically relevant time frame. Of the 15 patients enrolled, 10 cases had biopsies with adequate tumor content, and PDOs were successfully established in 4 of 10 cases. Drug profiling and genomic testing was completed in all established organoids, yielding an overall success rate of 40% in cases of biopsies with adequate tumor content. Drug sensitivity and genomic results were returned within 12 weeks and informed subsequent treatment selection in all evaluable cases. The primary endpoint - demonstrating that PDO-based drug screening combined with genomic characterization would identify clinically actionable outcomes in at least 46% of patients based on prior data - was not met. In conclusion, successful PDO establishment represents a limiting step in the implementation of FPO for metastatic breast cancer; however when PDO were successful, drug responses were always obtained and physicians chose to use the information in 100% of cases. These findings highlight the need for improved strategies optimizing use of patient biopsy material for drug testing in order to fully realize the clinical potential of FPO.
nfade2846f5a3: Sepsis mimics resemble sepsis clinically but may require different treatments. We evaluated whether inflammatory protein profiles could distinguish these conditions in a retrospective case-control study using 4 prospective Japanese cohorts. The study included 34 adults with sepsis and 46 with sepsis mimics. We measured 92 proteins using Olink, assessed between-group differences with false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment, and evaluated 3 prediction models using repeated nested cross-validation. No protein met the FDR threshold; the lowest FDR-adjusted P value was 0.345. The primary elastic-net model had an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.442 (95% confidence interval, 0.315-0.574), based on cross-validation predictions averaged for each participant. Random forest and gradient boosting also showed no clear evidence of discrimination above chance. Confidence intervals included chance performance in both the all-serum and quality-control-Pass sensitivity analyses. In this cohort, a single measurement of an inflammation-focused protein panel showed limited discrimination between sepsis and sepsis mimics. Integration with clinical information and longitudinal measurements warrants further investigation.
nfc61497720fb: Missense variant pathogenicity is usually interpreted according to the predicted effect on the protein via polypeptide alterations. But missense variants can also cause disease by disrupting RNA splicing, here defined as missense spliceogenic variants (MSVs). Although splice prediction is increasingly incorporated into variant classification pipelines, it is not a standardised process, so the scale and clinical relevance of MSVs remains poorly defined. We integrated whole-genome sequencing and circulating proteomic data from ~50,000 UK Biobank participants to characterise MSVs using ~8.3 million missense variants. We found that 2.7% of missense variants are predicted to alter splicing (SpliceAI {Delta} [≥] 0.2), comparable with synonymous variants (2.8%). Notably, 57% had benign/neutral AlphaMissense and REVEL scores (<0.34 and <0.5 respectively), rising to 85.2% in intrinsically disordered regions, indicating that many MSVs would not be prioritised by protein-centric predictors. MSVs were associated with reduced circulating levels of the cognate protein, approaching the effects of predicted loss-of-function variants. Analysis of raw SpliceAI scores revealed that events where novel cryptic sites outscored canonical sites resulted in the largest protein depletion, particularly when a premature frameshift was introduced. Validation of 14 predicted MSVs of uncertain significance in a clinical cohort provided strong pathogenic/likely pathogenic evidence, and screening unsolved cases from the 100,000 Genomes Project identified two novel candidate diagnostic MSVs. These findings establish the scale and functional consequences of MSVs, and demonstrate that RNA-centric interpretation can reveal clinically-relevant loss-of-function mechanisms missed by protein-centric missense variant interpretation.
n04b170978699: Title and abstract screening is among the most labor-intensive steps of systematic reviews. Jev, a low-cost AI decision model, scores records against eligibility criteria without screening labels. We scored 169,982 records from 128 reviews and, after tuning on development reviews, evaluated 23 held-out reviews once and 31 Cochrane reviews post hoc. Jev outranked the best free ranker in all 23 held-out reviews (mean AUC 0.966 vs 0.831) and came within 0.011 AUC of Claude Opus 5.5 on 1999 records at about 1/700 of its list-price cost (US$0.02/1000 records). Combined with active learning, it raised work saved at 95% recall from 0.659 to 0.806. A fixed score threshold fell below 95% recall in 3 of 28 Cochrane reviews, whereas Jev ranking with statistical stopping (post hoc) reached 95% recall in all 51 reviews, reading 86-88% of records. Label-free ranking with Jev was accurate and inexpensive, but stopping safely required screening decisions.
n832c131e2dc4: Importance: Pain varies in its intensity and course, yet much of our understanding of pain is based on cross-sectional assessments or longitudinal studies of selected clinical populations. Routinely collected electronic health record data may enable characterization of longitudinal pain patterns at scale. Objective: To identify longitudinal pain profiles among U.S. Veterans and characterize their clinical and polygenic correlates. Design: Cohort study using electronic health record and genomic data from the Million Veteran Program, with up to 16 years of pain assessments collected between 2000 to 2025. Setting: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs health care system. Participants: Million Veteran Program participants assigned to African-like, Admixed American-like, East Asian-like, European-like, or South Asian-like genetically inferred ancestry groups who have at least three years of outpatient numeric rating scale pain records. Exposures: Outpatient pain ratings and polygenic scores for psychiatric, sleep, and substance use traits. Main Outcomes and Measures: Pain profiles were identified using Gaussian finite mixture modeling of pain intensity, directional change, and within-person variability. Profiles were characterized by pain, psychiatric and substance use diagnoses, opioid exposure, body mass index, and polygenic scores. Results: Among 624,996 participants (Mean [SD] age at first pain rating=53.4 [13.5] years; 568,833 [91.0%] male), 51,731,567 outpatient pain ratings were analyzed. Three profiles were identified: stable no pain, stable mild pain, and mild-to-moderate increasing pain. Compared with the stable no pain profile, the increasing pain profile had higher odds of chronic pain (OR=21.14 [95% CI: 18.96-23.57]), opioid use disorder (OR=9.32 [95% CI: 8.31-10.45]), opioid exposure (OR=8.61 [95% CI: 8.41-8.83]), major depressive disorder (OR=3.77 [95% CI: 3.67-3.87]), and posttraumatic stress disorder (OR=3.72 [95% CI: 3.61-3.84]). Associations were attenuated but remained after adjustment for mean pain severity. Polygenic scores for depression, insomnia, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and tobacco use disorder were the most consistent predictors of increasing pain across the three largest genetically inferred ancestry groups. Conclusions and Relevance: Longitudinal modeling of routinely collected pain scores identified pain profiles associated with clinical burden and polygenic liability. These profiles captured clinically meaningful information beyond mean pain severity alone, highlighting the value of longitudinal pain phenotyping in electronic health record data.
n83a24d653ad3: Introduction Medicines account for 20% of the National Health Service (NHS) carbon footprint, but it is unclear how consistently they are measured by individual NHS trusts. This study assessed medicine carbon footprint (MCF) practices across NHS trusts in England and whether these changed between 2021 and 2024. Methods Freedom of Information requests were sent to NHS trusts about MCF practices in 2021 and 2024. Responses were analysed to determine the proportion of trusts calculating MCFs, the medicines included and the emission factors used for spend-based calculations. Reported spend-based factors were compared with the median factor for each year to assess the effect of factor choice on MCFs. Results Of 196 trusts included in analysis, 178 (91%) responded for 2021 and 182 (93%) for 2024. Among responding trusts, 30 of 178 calculated MCFs in 2021 compared with 46 of 182 in 2024. Spend-based medicine footprinting increased from 19 trusts in 2021 to 31 in 2024. Ten different factors were used by 15 trusts in 2021 and 13 by 21 trusts in 2024. Reported factors ranged from 31% below to 258% above the median in 2024. Conclusions Medicine carbon footprinting remained uncommon, with only one-quarter of responding NHS trusts calculating a footprint in 2024. Among trusts using spend-based methods, wide variation in emission factors produced substantially different estimated MCFs. Clear national guidance on spend-based methodology could improve consistency in the short term, while greater use of standardised product-level approaches may better support medicine decarbonisation over time.
nbd3b7f85c354: Up to one-third of Wilms tumours (WTs) arise in the context of genetic or epigenetic predisposition, but identifying predisposed patients remains challenging because germline variants can be missed due to variable clinical presentation, mosaicism, and cryptic variants. We tested whether tumour-derived molecular patterns can reveal underlying predisposition and thereby complement conventional diagnostic approaches. DNA methylation profiling of 138 WTs identified five molecular clusters that captured biological and predisposition-associated heterogeneity, including enrichment for Beckwith-Wiedemann Spectrum tumours, and a distinct WT1-driven subgroup. Cluster-guided reanalysis uncovered previously unrecognised WT1 pathogenic variants, including a newly identified germline variant that led to surveillance enrolment. A random forest classifier predicted WT1-driven tumours with ~90% accuracy across independent validation cohorts. Tumour methylation profiling identifies biologically and clinically relevant WT subgroups and reliably detects a WT1-driven tumour methylation signature. This approach can guide targeted variant reanalysis, and uncover clinically relevant germline variants missed by standard diagnostic workflows.
n42d29b6cefb3: Pooling cBioPortal studies into one patient-by-gene matrix is the standard preliminary to pan-cancer analysis, and the natural join key is the patient. Three Memorial Sloan Kettering clonal-hematopoiesis studies deposit blood normals carrying the same patient identifiers as tumors deposited elsewhere, so a patient-keyed merge records a hematopoietic clone as a mutation in that patients solid tumor. We linked 1,282,483 coding calls across 140 genes from 483 studies to patients, classified every call by specimen type, and rebuilt the matrix with and without blood-derived calls. Blood normals supply 1.7% of calls but concentrate sharply: 52.8% of patients flagged DNMT3A-mutant, 21.3% of TET2 and 19.7% of CHEK2 have no tumor-derived call in that gene, against 0.4% for TP53. The affected calls carry a clonal-hematopoiesis signature: DNMT3A supplies 42.0% of blood-normal and 0.61% of tumor calls, at a median allele fraction of 0.4% against 33.4%. The contamination reaches 65 other study cohorts, almost all of them solid-tumor studies, affecting more than one patient in ten in fifteen of them. It is a property of cohort composition rather than disease: across 45 cancer types the distortion tracks the share of patients with a paired blood normal at r = 0.994, and where one disease carries two unharmonized labels the rates differ up to fivefold before correction and agree after it. Correction lowers the pan-cancer DNMT3A rate by 45% and moves survival estimates further than chance removal of the same patients would. Two filter lines, applied before aggregation, remove it.
n055806ae072d: Background: Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) is increasingly used for treatment of locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) to improve treatment compliance, oncological outcomes and opportunities for organ preservation. However, evidence describing its implementation and outcomes in low- and middle-income countries remains limited. This study evaluated the feasibility, treatment delivery, oncological outcomes and organ preservation outcomes of TNT in a real-world South African setting. Methods: This was a retrospective review of a prospective cohort of adults with histologically confirmed, non-metastatic LARC treated with TNT at the Wits Donald Gordon Medical Centre, Johannesburg, between March 2022 and January 2026. Treatment was individualised following multidisciplinary review and included induction and/or consolidation systemic chemotherapy with either long- or short-course radiotherapy. Following TNT, treatment response was assessed clinically, endoscopically and radiologically. Patients with a clinical complete response (cCR) were offered watch-and-wait (WW) surveillance, while those with an incomplete response were recommended for total mesorectal excision (TME). The primary outcome was organ preservation, assessed as TME-free survival. Secondary outcomes included tumour regrowth, disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and local recurrence-free survival (LRFS) following TME. Results: Forty-six patients were included; median age was 63 years, 67.4% were male, 82.6% had T3-T4 tumours and 80.4% had node-positive disease. TNT was completed as planned in 95.7% of patients. Grade [≥]3 toxicity occurred in 19.5% during chemotherapy and 8.9% during radiotherapy. Twenty-one patients (45.7%) achieved a cCR and entered WW surveillance. TME-free survival was 46% (95% CI 31-60) at 1-year and 18% (95% CI 8-32) at 3-years. Three-year OS and DFS were 87% (95% CI 64-96) and 76% (95% CI 53-89), respectively. Among patients managed with WW, 3-year regrowth-free survival was 53% (95% CI 26-75). Three-year LRFS following TME was 94% (95% CI 68-99), and all patients undergoing TME or completed salvage surgery achieved an R0 resection. Conclusion: TNT was feasible and well tolerated in this real-world South African cohort, with high treatment completion and favourable medium-term oncological outcomes. Although almost half of patients initially achieved a cCR, declining TME-free and regrowth-free survival demonstrated that durable organ preservation was less frequent, highlighting the importance of structured surveillance and timely access to salvage surgery. These findings support the feasibility of delivering contemporary multimodal rectal cancer care in an appropriately resourced African setting.
nbf935500582e: Objective: Emotion dysregulation and irritability occur across pediatric disorders, complicating distinctions between general symptom burden and specific clinical presentations. Person-centered analyses can look at profiles of scores to identify groups with similar presentations. We examined whether modeling shared and domain-specific symptom variance identified differentiated profiles in youth. Method: Caregivers of 2,187 US youth ages 6-18 completed 87 items assessing emotion dysregulation, depression, mania-related symptoms, sleep-related impairment, and attention and behavioral problems. An ordinal bifactor model estimated one general and 13 specific factors. Latent profile analyses used standardized scores on all 14 factors, with an expanded raw-score analysis as a comparator. We examined caregiver-reported diagnoses and functioning and approximately two-week classification agreement among 166 recontacted caregivers. Results: The general factor accounted for 62% of common variance ({omega}H=.94), although model fit was mixed (CFI=.884; RMSEA=.058; SRMR=.092). A provisional four-class solution distinguished population-modal (67.4%), internalizing (11.8%), attention/hyperactivity (11.0%), and unusual-thought/elevated-mood (9.8%) profiles. Entropy was .83, but model enumeration and initialization checks did not establish a unique solution. Profiles showed overlapping diagnostic and functional correlates. Recontact agreement was 78.9% ({kappa}=.60). Irritability-specific reliability was limited, constraining interpretation of its weak profile differentiation. Conclusions: General symptom burden coexisted with differentiated residual symptom patterns. These findings support evaluating severity alongside symptom configuration, without equating profiles with diagnoses or weak residual irritability signals with limited clinical relevance. Measurement refinement, model-selection verification, and confirmation of classification-error-adjusted associations are needed before clinical application, but profiles could simplify clinical interpretation of sets of scales.
nb260192f4915: The prognostic relevance of peritumoral SULF1 transcript signal in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is unclear. We assembled a retrospective cohort of 133 patients with 218 primary-site tissue-microarray cores; 131 patients had evaluable boundary features. Multiplex fluorescence imaging combined RNAscope SULF1, CK-pan, and DAPI. Tumor-stroma boundaries were annotated with the SULF1 channel hidden. We screened 50 exported boundary features across cumulative stromal bands of 35-300 um against recurrence-free survival (RFS), overall survival (OS), and disease-specific survival (DSS), with false-discovery-rate correction. The strongest DSS association was signal SD within 150 um (n = 107; 23 disease-specific deaths; HR = 2.20 per SD; 95% CI, 1.64-2.94; q = 2.1 x 10^-6). In 50 repeated 5-fold cross-validations with feature selection repeated within training folds, adding a boundary feature to AJCC stage increased mean held-out DSS c-index from 0.613 to 0.754 (delta C = +0.141; 2.5th-97.5th percentiles across repeats, +0.105 to +0.192). These percentiles describe split variability, not confidence intervals. The 150-um SD feature was selected in 39.2% of DSS training folds. The DSS association persisted after adjustment for mean signal, although the measurements were strongly correlated. Peritumoral SULF1 signal dispersion was associated with outcome beyond an ordinal AJCC-stage model; independent validation is required.
nea12be3e04fd: The biomechanical properties of the human aorta play a key role in cardiovascular function and disease, yet their population-wide trends and variations remain largely unknown. To fill this crucial gap, we quantified variations in aortic size, stiffness and stresses across 57,434 individuals from the UK Biobank using two-dimensional cine MR imaging and a combined deep-learning, probabilistic and biomechanical modelling framework. Aortic diameter and distensibility (inverse of stiffness) were calculated for the ascending and descending aorta, and their conditional distributions were characterised as a function of age, sex, body size and blood pressure. These observations were integrated with ex-vivo tissue mechanics to infer stress distributions across the aortic wall and the associated uncertainty. Our analysis revealed several new relationships. Larger aortas were found to be stiffer, and greater body size (height and/or weight) was associated with larger aortas with no change in stiffness. Aortic distensibility was negatively associated with systolic, but not diastolic, blood pressure. Apparent sex differences in aortic size were substantially reduced after accounting for body size. Importantly, the maximum stress was found to depend not only on aortic size, as previously thought, but also on distensibility, with lower distensibility associated with higher stresses. The results provide first-of-their-kind population-scale reference distributions for human aortic stiffness, which will improve the personalisation of computational models and digital twins. The correlation between stress and distensibility strongly supports progressing beyond the current diameter-based criteria (based on the law of Laplace) and for the inclusion of stiffness in the clinical risk assessment of aortic diseases. Overall, this study forms the foundation for personalised quantitative medicine and biomechanically informed risk stratification of aortic aneurysms and dissections.
n5065c197eaf7: Background: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the prognostic value of Hippo signaling pathway biomarkers in oral squamous cell carcinoma. Methods: Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, electronic database searches identified 17 eligible studies involving 1,194 patients. Associations between the immunohistochemical expression of Hippo pathway effectors, primarily YAP and TAZ, and clinicopathological characteristics were assessed. Meta-analyses using random-effects models estimated pooled hazard ratios for overall survival. Results: Predominantly nuclear expression of YAP and TAZ was consistently associated with adverse clinicopathological features, including advanced clinical stage, lymph node metastasis, and poorer histological differentiation. Meta-analysis demonstrated that YAP overexpression was associated with worse overall survival (hazard ratio, 1.918; 95% confidence interval, 1.036 to 3.549; p = 0.038). TAZ overexpression was similarly associated with poorer overall survival (hazard ratio, 2.845; 95% confidence interval, 1.682 to 4.811; p < 0.001). Although substantial between-study heterogeneity was observed, the direction of the prognostic association remained consistent across studies. Conclusions: Increased nuclear expression of YAP and TAZ is consistently associated with more aggressive disease and poorer overall survival in oral squamous cell carcinoma. These findings support the prognostic value of Hippo pathway biomarkers, although methodological heterogeneity warrants cautious interpretation.
nf7ba6161756b: Consumer-grade wearables can continuously and longitudinally measure health signals such as heart rate (HR), activity, and sleep. While changes in these signals have been implicated in the early detection of infection (e.g., influenza, SARS-CoV-2) and real-time alerting systems have been developed, evidence from prospective deployment in pediatric transplant households remains limited. Here, we study the application of a resting heart rate (RHR)-based real-time alerting algorithm to detect respiratory virus infection in a cohort of solid organ transplant recipients and their household members (n=146) in a Phase IV clinical trial (NCT06161454). Reliable and efficient alerting for infection events may be particularly relevant for this population, enabling isolation, clinical management, and/or treatment. Of 31 antigen-test outcomes, nearly all (29/31, 93.5%) correspond to either influenza, COVID, or other patient-reported symptoms. We describe RHR, HR, activity, and sleep/circadian rhythm features around clinical alarm events, identifying candidate features for further investigation and algorithm improvement.
n1a3a5bd5e4d3: Background: In coastal Bangladesh, saline drinking water has been linked to raised blood pressure. The 2025 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) measured electrical conductivity (EC), a salinity indicator, in source water, but its report gave no population counts or district estimates. Objectives: To estimate how many people live in households whose tested source has high EC, and to describe patterns by place, household characteristics, source type and arsenic. Methods. EC was measured in source water of 6,040 households in 64 districts, February to June. In 14.5% of households the tested source was not the main drinking-water source. Primary outcomes were EC above 1,500 and 3,000 microsiemen/cm, survey risk classes that are not health-based standards. Estimates were survey weighted; comparisons were observational. Results: EC exceeded 1,500 microsiemen/cm in 5.3% of households (95% CI 4.7 to 5.9), about 9.0 million people, including 1.8 million above 3,000 microsiemen/cm. Coastal-zone districts held 26% of households but 70% of those above 1,500 microsiemen/cm. Shares varied little by wealth or in households with young children or pregnant women. Nationally, deep tube wells more often had high EC because most are coastal. In the coastal zone, deep and shallow wells had similar shares (16.1% and 17.9%). After district adjustment, EC was about 18% lower in deep wells (geometric mean ratio 0.82, 0.73 to 0.92). Within upazilas (restricted sample) it was 0.93 (0.80 to 1.07). Arsenic above 10 ppb was more common where EC was high, but this link weakened after district adjustment. Conclusions: Millions of people live in households whose tested source has high EC, mostly in coastal and south-central districts. Deep wells had modestly lower EC after geographic adjustment, but the difference shrank within upazilas and depended on the handling of implausibly low readings. The findings support measuring EC alongside arsenic, with documented meter calibration.
n8d070c805b38: Background In Kenya, stroke is one of the top five causes of mortality, with a high rate of inpatient mortality. The American Heart Association (AHA) and American Stroke Association (ASA) translated scientific evidence into evidence-based clinical practice guidelines aimed at reducing inpatient mortality and improving the quality of care for stroke patients. Despite the proven benefits of the ASA stroke guidelines in improving stroke care, translation of the guidelines in various settings remains a key challenge. This study aimed to quantify the gap between evidence-based recommendations and current stroke care practices in a peri-urban referral facility in Kiambu, Kenya. The study was conducted at xxxxxxxxxx Hospital, a peri-urban referral facility in Kiambu County, Kenya. Methods: We reviewed records of stroke patients attending xxxxxxxxxxx from January 1, 2020, to December 31, 2023. The study evaluated acute stroke management practices and secondary prevention against the 2019 American Heart Association/American Stroke Association (AHA/ASA) Guidelines for the Early Management of Acute Ischemic Stroke. Results: The median distance travelled by stroke patients to the facility was 47.8 kilometres; further, the median onset-to-presentation time was 24 hours. The study evaluated eight clinical practices against the ASA guidelines. The facility lacked a dedicated stroke unit. Remarkably, patients arriving within the therapeutic window for intravenous alteplase and thrombectomy did not receive these treatments. Secondary prevention measures, including discharge on an antiplatelet regimen, were moderately adhered to; among the 86 eligible ischemic stroke patients, 67 (77.9%) were correctly discharged on aspirin. Similarly, 84/123 (68.3%) of the patients were discharged on statin therapy. Conclusion: Evidence-based stroke care recommendations were minimally adhered to at this peri-urban referral facility in Kiambu, Kenya. Contribution: This study quantifies the gap between evidence-based stroke care recommendations and current clinical practice in a peri-urban referral facility in Kenya, providing context-specific evidence to inform quality improvement initiatives and guideline implementation efforts in similar resource-constrained settings.
n8b5219457037: This paper shows that it is possible to predict which newly published biomedical research papers will be connected to subsequent clinical trials. We use CAR-T cell therapy as a proof-of-concept setting because its development can be followed from published research through clinical testing, regulatory approval, and commercialization. We reconstructed connections between research papers and clinical trials and trained machine-learning models to predict which papers were associated with research that progressed to clinical testing. Using 65 paper-inherent indicators, including scientific topic, language, biomedical orientation, and team structure, the models achieved a cross-validated AUC of 0.908. The resulting rankings were also practically informative. In a retrospective analysis using no information generated after 2016, 80% of the top 20 papers came from laboratories associated with one of 13 predefined major CAR-T clinical or commercial outcomes. As an additional finding, first-year citations alone achieved an AUC of 0.797, while provenance indicators based on author, journal, and institutional reputation performed less strongly and added little to the paper-inherent model. Our results show that whether biomedical research papers will be connected to subsequent clinical trials can be predicted from newly published papers with high discrimination in CAR-T. Our findings could help research organizations and pharmaceutical companies identify papers, laboratories, and therapeutic programs that warrant closer evaluation before clinical outcomes are known.
n234eeedd2492: The upper cervical spinal cord is essential for motor, sensory and autonomic function, yet its normative morphometric trajectories and disease-related deviations remain unclear. Using three-dimensional T1-weighted images from 10,159 healthy individuals aged 8-85 years, we established normative references for averaged and level-specific upper cervical spinal cord morphometry, revealing measure-specific trajectories with peak ages of 29.7-44.1 years. These references were applied to 2,394 patients with seven neurological disorders: mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer' s disease, Parkinson' s disease, cerebral small vessel disease, multiple sclerosis, neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease to derive individualized deviation scores. These deviation scores captured disease-specific abnormalities, enabled disease classification, and were associated with cognition, physical disability and disease progression. Finally, a personalized upper cervical spinal cord report was developed to support individualized imaging interpretation. Together, these findings provide a normative framework for quantifying upper cervical spinal cord morphometry and advancing personalized assessment across neurological disorders.
nc48284bab888: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) has traditionally been viewed as one of the most chronic psychiatric disorders. Although longitudinal studies have demonstrated promising rates of symptomatic remission, recovery and other clinical outcome measures often remain comparatively low. Qualitative research offers an important perspective on how individuals with BPD may extend a more representative view of improvement and change. We collected narratives from 41 participants with a self-reported diagnosis of BPD and analyzed them using thematic analysis. Its national, virtual recruitment approach enabled a relatively large qualitative sample diverse in gender identity, age, U.S. geographic region, treatment history, and current clinical severity, extending the range of perspectives represented in prior work. Three central themes were identified. The first, Differing attitudes toward language, reflected participants’experiences of recovery language as paradoxically both validating and stigmatizing. While individual language preferences varied, participants generally converged on a sharedunderstanding of what recovery meant to them. The second, Recovery as a dynamic and relational process, described recovery as nonlinear, effortful, and closely tied to interpersonal experiences. The third, Crossroads and uneven change over time, highlighted the role of personal agency, critical decision points in seeking treatment, and the persistence of internal distress even as behavioral symptoms improve. Findings from this study both replicate and extend existing qualitative research by discussing how individuals with BPD understand recovery in ways that may not be captured by traditional clinical outcome measures. These results emphasize the importance of incorporating lived-experience perspectives when defining recovery and setting treatment goals.
ndaf72b70cc08: Background: Patient-facing AI intake chatbots can enter clinical use without regulatory review, so their errors may first surface with actual patients. Objective: To develop and pilot a remote, voice-based standardized patient (SP) method for evaluating an intake chatbot's history-taking, documentation, and patient-centeredness. Methods: Four primary care cases had Easy and Difficult variants. In Phase 1, five SPs completed 40 encounters with internal medicine residents rating portrayal fidelity. In Phase 2, SPs completed 80 encounters with a ChatGPT 4o chatbot, recorded whether critical elements were asked about and addressed satisfactorily, and rated summaries; four debriefing interviews were analyzed. In Phase 3, two blinded clinicians rated transcripts and summaries from 101 encounters (32 resident-led, 69 chatbot-led). Results: Portrayal fidelity averaged 4.52 of 5. The chatbot asked about 59.3% of critical elements in Easy versus 50.2% in Difficult variants (adjusted OR 1.49; 95% CI, 1.15 to 1.93) and addressed 73.3% versus 64.6% (OR 1.47; 1.12 to 1.93); near-ceiling summary quality did not differ. SPs reported missed information and rushed pacing. Reviewer agreement was moderate to substantial for element judgments (AC1 0.49 to 0.70) but poor for totals (ICC 0.10 and 0.21). In exploratory comparisons, residents asked about more elements (adjusted difference 12.5 percentage points; 95% CI, 7.0 to 18.1) and satisfactorily addressed more (9.2 points; 3.8 to 14.6); totals did not differ. Conclusions: SP portrayal was consistent enough for pre-clinical chatbot evaluation, and the method detected lower coverage in harder cases. Documentation ratings alone may miss conversational gaps, which require direct measurement.
n3304675f6123: Background: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by persistent symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity that significantly affect cognitive, academic, and social functioning. Although electroencephalography (EEG) has emerged as a promising non-invasive tool for identifying objective neurophysiological biomarkers of ADHD because of its high temporal resolution and cost-effectiveness, many existing machine learning studies rely on single-domain EEG features, which may not adequately capture the complex functional organization of the brain. Methods: This study proposes a subject-level EEG classification framework that integrates three complementary feature domains: spectral characteristics, weighted Phase Lag Index (wPLI)-based functional connectivity, and topological descriptors derived from persistent homology. EEG recordings from 121 subjects were preprocessed and segmented into overlapping windows for feature extraction. Window-level features were aggregated to generate subject-level representations. Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) was employed to select the 110 most informative features from an initial set of 1,043 descriptors. Five machine learning classifiers, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), were evaluated using stratified five-fold cross-validation. An ablation study was further conducted to assess the contribution of each feature domain. Model interpretability was investigated using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME), two widely adopted Explainable Artificial Intelligence techniques for interpreting machine learning models. Results: Among the evaluated classifiers, the SVM achieved the highest classification performance, yielding an accuracy of 80.17%, an F1-score of 80.95%, a balanced accuracy of 80.14%, a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) of 86.72%, and a precision recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) of 87.34%. The ablation study demonstrated that combining spectral, functional connectivity, and topological features consistently outperformed individual feature domains, highlighting the complementary nature of these representations. Explainable AI analyses further identified functional connectivity features as the primary contributors to classification performance while confirming the additional value of spectral and topological descriptors. Conclusions: The proposed framework demonstrates that integrating spectral analysis, functional connectivity, and topological data analysis provides an effective and interpretable approach for subject-level ADHD classification from EEG recordings. The combination of recursive feature selection, multi-domain feature fusion, ablation analysis, and Explainable Artificial Intelligence establishes a transparent and reproducible pipeline that may facilitate the development of reliable EEG-based clinical decision-support systems for ADHD.
n586b4c648cb9: Background Heart rate fragmentation (HRF) has emerged as a novel marker of sinoatrial instability and neuroautonomic dysregulation and is a predictor of incident cardiovascular disease (CVD) events and cardiovascular mortality. Leveraging heart rate fragmentation as a novel measure may help us better understand the prognostic significance of physical activity. Physical activity (PA) patterns are multidimensional and difficult to study holistically, however. We sought to examine for novel PA clusters in a cohort of veteran men and evaluate their prognostic significance based on their associations with neuroautonomic dysregulation. Methods In this cross-sectional study, we examined 602 male veterans from the Vietnam Era Twins Study of Electrophysiology in Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (VETS-EP) who were enrolled between 2022 and 2026. Accelerometry data were used to derive physical activity parameters across 6 domains: volume, sedentary behavior, intensity, diurnal pattern, fragmentation, and variability. Heart rate fragmentation was assessed using percentage of inflection points (PIP), inverse average length of segments (IALS), percentage of short segments (PSS), and percentage of alternating segments (PAS). Gaussian mixture models were used to derive digital phenotypes of physical activity, and associations with heart rate fragmentation were assessed using linear mixed models. Results Participants had a mean age of 73.8 {+/-} 2.9 years and 93.2% reported White race. Two overlapping phenotypes of physical activity patterns were identified: a compact-early phenotype, characterized by earlier activity timing and slightly greater overall activity, and a diffuse-late phenotype, characterized by later activity timing and greater heterogeneity in activity volume. In fully adjusted models, the diffuse-late phenotype was associated with higher PIP, the primary outcome ({beta}: 1.199, 95% CI: 0.034 to 2.363, p-value: 0.044), and higher IALS ({beta}: 0.01210, 95% CI: 0.00048 to 0.02373, p-value: 0.041), but not PSS or PAS, compared with the compact-early phenotype. Conclusions In older male veterans, Gaussian mixture model phenotyping identified two overlapping physical activity phenotypes, differing mainly in diurnal timing and in the dispersion of overall activity, that were associated with modest differences in heart rate fragmentation. These phenotypes provide a framework for capturing complex physical activity patterns. Future prospective studies representing diverse populations are needed to validate such phenotypes.
n0e9e536cfb21: Background: The Lung Transplant Frailty Scale (LT-FS) is a validated binary measure of frailty in lung transplant candidates. We aimed to refine the LT-FS Base and Body Composition measures by developing a three-category classification to improve clinical risk stratification with serum albumin as a more clinically practical frailty biomarker. Methods: To develop the refined LT-FS, we applied a 4-step measure development method to a multicenter prospective cohort study of lung transplant candidates. Low albumin (<3.5 g/dL) replaced high serum C-reactive protein ([≥]10 mg/L) as the LT-FS biomarker. Cutpoints that balanced discrimination, risk prediction, and calibration were identified to define ''frail'', ''pre-frail'', and ''not frail'' categories. Next, we evaluated associations between the refined LT-FS and exercise capacity, patient-reported outcomes, and mortality using multivariate linear and Cox regression. Results: Among 419 participants, the refined LT-FS identified a graded increase in mortality risk across frailty categories. For example, compared with candidates who were not frail, pre-frailty and frailty by the LT-FS Body Composition were associated with a 2.9-fold (HR 2.9, 95% CI 1.2-6.9) and 7-fold (HR 6.9, 95% CI 2.6-18.2) higher risk of waitlist delisting or death, respectively. Pre-frailty and frailty by LT-FS Body Composition were associated with 2-fold (HR 2.1, 95% CI 1.2-3.8) and 3.6-fold (HR 3.6, 95% CI 1.8-7.3) higher risk of mortality after transplant. Relationships with exercise capacity and patient-reported disability were less consistent. Conclusions: A refined Lung Transplant Frailty Scale incorporating serum albumin demonstrates strong associations with waitlist and post-transplant mortality. The addition of a pre-frail category better captures the continuum of frailty and improves clinical risk stratification of lung transplant candidates.
nb54213e125d9: Background. Classical macroparasite models commonly represent worm burden heterogeneity through prescribed Poisson or negative-binomial (NB) distributions, while transmission dynamics are formulated in terms of aggregate quantities such as mean worm burden and prevalence. We revisit these assumptions using a stratified worm burden (SWB) framework that explicitly tracks the distribution of parasite burdens across heterogeneous host classes and allows demographic turnover, transmission, and interventions to be analyzed within a unified model. Methods. We derive equilibrium distributions of the SWB system under homogeneous and heterogeneous infection processes and compare them with the classical Poisson and NB distributions used in macroparasite epidemiology and control policymaking. The framework is then extended to include host demography, coupled human-snail transmission dynamics, and periodic mass drug administration (MDA). Corresponding SWB and NB-type MacDonald models are calibrated to comparable endemic prevalence and mean worm burden, allowing direct comparison of potential transmission breakpoints and intervention outcomes. Results. In the absence of demographic turnover, the SWB framework naturally generates Poisson and NB equilibrium distributions as limiting cases of homogeneous and heterogeneous infection processes. Incorporating demographic recruitment and mortality alters these benchmark distributions, producing endemic burden structures that differ systematically from their classical counterparts. Analysis of coupled human-snail systems reveals that transmission breakpoints and bistable equilibria occur only within a relatively restricted region of SWB parameter space. In contrast, comparable NB-MacDonald formulations exhibit breakpoint behavior over substantially broader parameter ranges with the net effect of overestimating the likelihood of interruption of transmission. Although calibrated models can reproduce near identical endemic prevalence and mean worm burden, they often generate markedly different responses to MDA, including differences in rebound dynamics, persistence, and elimination thresholds. Conclusions. The SWB framework links classical statistical descriptions of worm aggregation to mechanistic burden-resolved population dynamics, clarifying how endemic distributions emerge and how they are modified by demography and control interventions. Our results suggest that transmission breakpoints are not a universal feature of helminth systems but depend strongly on model structure, and that predictions of elimination and post-treatment recovery may be considerably more model-dependent than implied by prevalence-based calibration alone. The SWB approach therefore provides a flexible alternative framework for evaluating parasite transmission dynamics and predicting the outcomes of control strategies.
